sentences.zh: 袁紹

translations.literal: Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao.

translations.literal: Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Part Two.

sentences.zh: 譚自稱車騎將軍，出軍黎陽。

translations.literal: Tan styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry and marched his army out to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan proclaimed himself General of Chariots and Cavalry and led his troops to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 尚少與其兵，而使逢紀隨之。

translations.literal: Shang gave him few troops and sent Feng Ji to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang allotted him scant forces and assigned Feng Ji to go with him.

sentences.zh: 譚求益兵，審配等又議不與。

translations.literal: Tan requested additional troops; Shen Pei and others again deliberated and would not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Tan asked for more men, Shen Pei and his faction met again and refused.

sentences.zh: 譚怒，殺逢紀。

translations.literal: Tan was angry and killed Feng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yuan Tan had Feng Ji put to death.

sentences.zh: 曹操度河攻譚，譚告急於尚，尚乃留審配守鄴，自將助譚，與操相拒於黎陽。

translations.literal: Cao Cao crossed the river and attacked Tan; Tan reported urgency to Shang; Shang thereupon left Shen Pei to defend Ye, himself led troops to aid Tan, and faced Cao at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao crossed the Yellow River to strike Yuan Tan, who urgently appealed to Yuan Shang. Yuan Shang left Shen Pei to hold Ye, took command himself to reinforce his brother, and opposed Cao Cao at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 自九月至明年二月，大戰城下，[一]譚、尚敗退。

translations.literal: From the ninth month until the second month of the next year they fought greatly beneath the walls; [one] Tan and Shang were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: From the ninth month through the second month of the following year they fought fiercely under the city walls; Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 操將圍之，乃夜遁還鄴。

translations.literal: Cao was about to surround them; they then fled by night back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao was closing in to besiege them, they slipped away by night and returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 操進軍，尚逆擊破操，操軍還許，譚謂尚曰：「我鎧甲不精，故前為曹操所敗。

translations.literal: Cao advanced his army; Shang met him in attack and defeated Cao; Cao's army returned to Xu. Tan said to Shang, "My armor was not fine; therefore earlier I was defeated by Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pressed forward, but Yuan Shang counterattacked and routed him, so Cao's army fell back to Xu. Yuan Tan told Yuan Shang, "My armor was poor—that is why Cao Cao defeated me before.

sentences.zh: 今操軍退，人懷歸志，及其未濟，出兵掩之，可令大潰，此策不可失也。

translations.literal: Now Cao's army has withdrawn; the men harbor thoughts of returning home. Before they have crossed, send out troops to fall upon them—you can make them suffer a great rout. This plan must not be missed."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Cao's men are retreating, every soldier is thinking of home. Strike them before they finish the crossing and you can shatter them utterly. We cannot let this chance slip."

sentences.zh: 」尚疑而不許，既不益兵，又不易甲。

translations.literal: " Shang doubted and did not consent; he neither increased troops nor replaced armor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang hesitated and refused: he sent no reinforcements and issued no new armor.

sentences.zh: 譚大怒，郭圖、辛評因此謂譚曰：「使先公出將軍為兄後者，皆是審配之所構也。

translations.literal: Tan was greatly angry. Guo Tu and Xin Ping therefore said to Tan, "That the late lord made the general heir after your elder brother was all plotting by Shen Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan was furious. Guo Tu and Xin Ping seized the moment to tell him, "Shen Pei is the one who arranged for your late father to pass you over in favor of your elder brother."

sentences.zh: 」譚然之。

translations.literal: " Tan assented to it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan believed them.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵攻尚，戰於外門。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops to attack Shang and fought at the outer gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against Yuan Shang and gave battle at the outer gate of the city wall.

sentences.zh: [二]譚敗，乃引兵還南皮。

translations.literal: [Two] Tan was defeated; thereupon he led troops back to Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan lost the fight and withdrew his army to Nanpi.

sentences.zh: [三] 注[一]郭緣生《述征記》曰：「黎陽城西袁譚城，城南又有一城，是曹公攻譚之所築。」

translations.literal: [Three] Commentary note [one]: Guo Yuansheng's Record of Campaigns says, "West of Liyang city is Yuan Tan's fort; south of the city there is another fort, which Duke Cao built when he attacked Tan."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Guo Yuansheng's Record of Campaigns states: west of Liyang lies Yuan Tan's enclosure, and south of the city stands another rampart that Cao Cao threw up during his campaign against Yuan Tan.

sentences.zh: 注[二]郛郭之門。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: The gate of the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: the gate in the outer rampart.

sentences.zh: 注[三]南皮，今滄州縣也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: Nanpi is a county of modern Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: Nanpi is in present-day Cangzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 章武有北皮亭，故此曰南皮。

translations.literal: Zhangwu has Beipi pavilion; therefore this is called Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhangwu district has a Beipi pavilion, this place is called Nanpi, "South Pi."

sentences.zh: 別駕王修率吏人自青州往救譚，譚還欲更攻尚，問修曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: Adjutant Administrator Wang Xiu led clerks and people from Qingzhou to go rescue Tan; Tan further wished again to attack Shang and asked Xiu, saying, "What plan will come forth?
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Administrator Wang Xiu brought officials and men from Qingzhou to Yuan Tan's relief. Yuan Tan then wanted to strike Yuan Shang again and asked Wang Xiu, "What course should we take?

sentences.zh: 」修曰：

translations.literal: " Xiu said:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu replied:

sentences.zh: 「兄弟者，左右手也。

translations.literal: " Brothers are like left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: "Brothers are a man's two hands.

sentences.zh: 譬人將□而斷其右手，曰『我必勝若』，如是者可乎？

translations.literal: It is like someone about to fight and cutting off his own right hand, saying 'I am sure to defeat you'—may it be so?
translations.idiomatic: It is as if a man about to go into battle hacked off his own right hand and cried, 'Now I am bound to win!' Could anything be more absurd?

sentences.zh: 夫□兄弟而不親，天下其誰親之？

translations.literal: Now [lacuna] brothers and not being close—whom in the world would they be close to?
translations.idiomatic: If you spurn your own brothers, whom under heaven would you treat as kin?

sentences.zh: 屬有讒人交□其閒，以求一朝之利，願塞耳勿聽也。

translations.literal: Recently there have been slanderers mixing [lacuna] between them to seek advantage for a morning—wish to plug the ears and not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men have lately come between you to profit from a single morning's quarrel; I pray you shut your ears and pay them no heed.

sentences.zh: 若斬佞臣數人，復相親睦，以御四方，可橫行於天下。

translations.literal: If you behead several flatterers and again are mutually close and harmonious, to resist the four directions, you can course horizontally across the world.
translations.idiomatic: Execute a handful of flatterers, heal the breach between you, and face the realm together—you could stride anywhere under heaven unopposed.

sentences.zh: 」譚不從。

translations.literal: " Tan did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 尚復自將攻譚，譚戰大敗，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Shang again personally led troops to attack Tan; Tan fought and was greatly defeated, encircling the city and firmly defending.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang took the field once more against his brother. Yuan Tan suffered a crushing defeat and pulled back behind his walls.

sentences.zh: [一]尚圍之急，譚奔平原，而遣穎川辛毗詣曹操請救。

translations.literal: [One] Shang surrounded him urgently; Tan fled to Pingyuan and sent Yingchuan Xin Pi to go to Cao Cao to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuan Shang tightened the siege, Yuan Tan fled to Pingyuan and dispatched Xin Pi of Yingchuan to beg Cao Cao for aid.

sentences.zh: [二] 注[一]《前書》蒯通曰：「必將嬰城固守。

translations.literal: [Two] Commentary note [one]: The Former Documents: Kuai Tong said, "They are sure to encircle the city and firmly defend.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: The Han Shu records Kuai Tong saying, "They will certainly cling to their walls and hold fast.

sentences.zh: 」音義曰：「嬰謂以城自繞也。」

translations.literal: " Sounds and Meanings says: "Ying means to wrap oneself with the city.""
translations.idiomatic: The Sounds and Meanings gloss explains ying as "to coil the city around oneself like a belt."

sentences.zh: 注[二]魏志曰：「辛毗，穎川陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: The Wei Records says: "Xin Pi was a man of Yangzhai in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: The Records of Wei states that Xin Pi came from Yangzhai in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 譚使毗詣太祖求和，毗見太祖致譚意。

translations.literal: Tan sent Pi to go to the Grand Progenitor to seek peace; Pi saw the Grand Progenitor and conveyed Tan's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan sent Xin Pi to the imperial protector to sue for peace, and Xin Pi laid out Yuan Tan's terms.

sentences.zh: 太祖悅，謂毗曰：『譚可信，尚必可克不？

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said to Pi, "Can Tan be trusted—will Shang surely be able to be overcome or not?"
translations.idiomatic: The protector was pleased and asked Xin Pi, "Can we trust Yuan Tan? And can Yuan Shang be broken?"

sentences.zh: 』毗對曰：『明公無問信與詐也，直*

translations.literal: " Pi replied: "Illustrious lord, do not ask about trust or deceit; simply—
translations.idiomatic: Xin Pi answered, "My lord, set aside the question of sincerity—simply

translations.literal: (say)
translations.idiomatic: (Explanation)

sentences.zh: *當論其埶耳。

translations.literal: * ought to discuss their situation, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: consider how the balance of power lies.

sentences.zh: 袁氏本兄弟相伐，非謂他人能閒其閒，乃謂天下可定於己也。

translations.literal: The Yuans originally attacked one another as brothers—not meaning others could sow discord between them, but meaning the realm could be settled by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan tore at one another not because outsiders could drive a wedge, but because each brother imagined he alone could master the empire.

sentences.zh: 一旦求救於明公，此可知也。

translations.literal: Once they seek rescue from the illustrious lord—this can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Now that one of them pleads for your help, the truth is plain.

sentences.zh: 』」劉表以書諫譚曰：

translations.literal: (End of quotation.) Liu Biao sent a letter remonstrating Tan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: With Xin Pi's audience concluded, Liu Biao addressed a letter of remonstrance to Yuan Tan:

sentences.zh: 天降災害，禍難殷流，初交殊族，卒成同盟，使王室震盪，彝倫攸斁。

translations.literal: Heaven sends calamities; disasters flow thickly. Those who first dealt with outside houses and then formed a league have shaken the throne and brought the moral norms to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends calamity; misfortune spreads unchecked. Men of different houses who first stood apart and then swore alliance have convulsed the royal house and shattered the moral order.

sentences.zh: [一]是以智達之士，莫不痛心入骨，傷時人不能相忍也。

translations.literal: [One] Therefore perspicacious gentlemen all ache to the marrow and grieve that men of the age cannot bear with one another.
translations.idiomatic: Every thoughtful observer feels the grief down to the bone and mourns that our contemporaries cannot endure one another.

sentences.zh: 然孤與太公，志同願等，[二] 雖楚魏絕邈，山河迥遠，[三]戮力乃心，共□王室，[四]使非族不干吾盟，異類不絕吾好，此孤與太公無貳之所致也。

translations.literal: Yet I and the Grand Duke had the same aim and equal wishes; [two] although Chu and Wei were vastly apart and mountains and rivers lay remote, [three] we joined strength in heart and together aided the royal house; [four] we caused alien clans not to violate our covenant and foreign peoples not to sever our goodwill—this is what issued from my and the Grand Duke's having no divided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your father and I were of one mind and one purpose: though Jingzhou and Ji province stood far apart, we bent every effort to uphold the house of Han, kept outsiders from breaking our league, and barred barbarians from sundering our friendship—that was the single-hearted compact between your father and me.

sentences.zh: 功績未卒，太公殂隕，賢胤承統，以繼洪業。

translations.literal: Their merit was not finished when the Grand Duke died; worthy heirs received the succession to continue the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: That great work was still unfinished when your father passed away; worthy sons took up his mandate to carry the enterprise forward.

sentences.zh: 宣奕世之德，履丕顯之祚，[五]摧嚴敵於鄴都，揚休烈於朔土，顧定疆宇，虎視河外，凡我同盟，莫不景附。

translations.literal: They displayed virtue accumulated through generations and trod the glorious mandate; [five] they crushed a formidable enemy at Ye, raised splendid merit on the northern soil, looked back to secure the territory, and glared like tigers beyond the Yellow River—every one of our covenant allies none failed to admire and attach.
translations.idiomatic: They unfolded virtues piled up over generations and walked in a dazzling mandate: they shattered a dreaded foe at Ye, spread glorious deeds across the northern plain, steadied the borders, and glared beyond the river while every ally rallied to them in awe.

sentences.zh: 何悟青蠅飛於竿旌，無忌游於二壘，[六]使股肱分成二體，匈膂絕為異身。

translations.literal: Who would have thought bluebottle flies would alight on the pennants and Wuji roam between two ramparts—[six] causing arms and thighs to split into two bodies and chest and back to be severed into different persons?
translations.idiomatic: Who could have foreseen slanderers lighting on your banners like bluebottle flies, or a Wuji flitting between two camps—twin arms torn from one torso, heart and backbone turned against each other?

sentences.zh: 初聞此問，尚謂不然，定聞信來，乃知閼伯、實沈之忿已成，□親即讎之計已決，[七]旃□交於中原，暴屍累於城下。

translations.literal: At first hearing this news I still thought it not so; when reliable word arrived I knew the rancor of Ebo and Shenshi was already complete and the plan to treat kin as enemies was settled—[seven] banners and drums clash in the central plain, exposed corpses pile beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When I first heard the rumor I hoped it was false; credible messengers have since convinced me that the feud of Ebo and Shenshi is upon you, that kinsmen have resolved to meet as foes, that war drums roll across the heartland, and that the dead lie heaped below your walls.

sentences.zh: 聞之哽咽，若存若亡。

translations.literal: Hearing it I choke with grief, as if alive as if dead.
translations.idiomatic: The news leaves me speechless with sorrow, half convinced I am dreaming.

sentences.zh: 昔三王、五伯，下及戰國，君臣相弒，父子相殺，兄弟相殘，親戚相滅，蓋時有之。

translations.literal: Formerly the Three Kings and Five Hegemons, down to the Warring States—lords and ministers slew one another, fathers and sons killed one another, brothers mauled one another, kinsmen destroyed one another—such things occurred from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dynasties and Five Hegemons through the Warring States, rulers murdered ministers, fathers slew sons, brothers cut one another down, and whole clans were erased—history knows such seasons.

sentences.zh: 然或欲以成王業，[八]或欲以定霸功，[九]皆所謂逆取順守，而徼富強於一世也。

translations.literal: Yet some wished thereby to complete kingly enterprise, [eight] some wished thereby to settle hegemonic merit—[nine] all are what is called seizing in rebellion and holding in obedience, seeking wealth and strength for one generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some pursued legitimate kingship, others hegemonic sway—all aimed at winning power by bold strokes and keeping it by righteousness, and sought lasting strength for their age.

sentences.zh: 未有□親即異，兀其根本，而能全於長世者也。

translations.literal: Never has one who treated kin as strangers and cut his root been able to preserve himself through long generations.
translations.idiomatic: No house that casts off blood ties and hacks at its own roots has endured for generations.

sentences.zh: 注[一]左傳曰：「震盪播越。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: The Zuo Commentary says: "They shook the realm and scattered into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: the Zuo Commentary reads, "They convulsed the altars and fled abroad."

sentences.zh: 」書曰：「彝倫攸斁。

translations.literal: " The Documents says: "The constant norms thereby collapsed."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents adds, "The eternal moral pattern was thrown into ruin."

sentences.zh: 」彝，常也。

translations.literal: " Yi means constant.
translations.idiomatic: Yi means "constant."

sentences.zh: 倫，理也。

translations.literal: Lun means pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Lun means "ordering principle."

sentences.zh: 攸，所也。

translations.literal: You means the place.
translations.idiomatic: You is the classical particle for "thereby" or "whereby."

sentences.zh: 斁，敗也。

translations.literal: Yi means ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi means "to ruin" or "to overthrow."

sentences.zh: 注[二]言太公者尊之，謂紹也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Speaking "Grand Duke" is honoring him—it refers to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: the title "Grand Duke" is an honorific for Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 注[三]楚，荊州也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: Chu is Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: "Chu" here means Jing province.

sentences.zh: 魏，冀州也。

translations.literal: Wei is Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: "Wei" stands for Ji province in the north.

sentences.zh: 注[四]左傳曰：「同好惡，□王室。

translations.literal: Commentary note [four]: The Zuo Commentary says: "Share likes and dislikes, [lacuna] the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 4: the Zuo Commentary counsels men to "share loves and hates and jointly sustain the house of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」杜預曰：「□，助也。」

translations.literal: " Du Yu says: "[Lacuna] means assist.""
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu glosses the missing graph as "to aid."

sentences.zh: 注[五]奕，重也，國語曰「奕代載德」。

translations.literal: Commentary note [five]: Yi means layered; the Discourses of the States says "generations piled high bearing virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 5: yi means "layer upon layer"; the Discourses speaks of "age after age laden with virtue."

sentences.zh: 注[六]詩小雅曰：「營營青蠅，止於榛。

translations.literal: Commentary note [six]: An ode in the "Lesser Elegantiae" says: "Buzzing fly upon the hazel grove.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 6: the "Blueflies" poem runs, "Buzzing bluebottles settle on the hazel hedge."

sentences.zh: 讒人罔極，構我二人。

translations.literal: Slanderers without limit embroil us two."
translations.idiomatic: "Scheming men know no restraint; they set the two of us at odds."

sentences.zh: 」史記，費無忌得寵於楚平王，為太子建少傅，無寵於太子，日夜讒太子於王，欲誅太子。

translations.literal: " The Records: Fei Wuji gained favor with King Ping of Chu, became junior tutor to heir-apparent Jian—had no favor with the heir—and day and night slandered the heir to the king, wishing to execute the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Records relate how Fei Wuji curried favor with King Ping of Chu, served as junior tutor to Crown Prince Jian yet earned no trust from him, and ceaselessly poisoned the king's ear until he sought the prince's death.

sentences.zh: 太子亡奔宋。

translations.literal: The heir fled to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince fled to Song for his life.

sentences.zh: 左傳作「無極」。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary writes "Wuji."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary spells his name Wuji.

sentences.zh: 竿旌、二壘者，謂譚、尚也。

translations.literal: "Pennants" and "two ramparts" refer to Tan and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The "pennants" and "twin camps" stand for Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang.

sentences.zh: 注[七]左傳子產曰：「高辛氏有二子，伯曰閼伯，季曰實沈，居於曠林，不相能也，日尋干戈，以相征討。」

translations.literal: Commentary note [seven]: Zichan in the Zuo Commentary says: "Gaoxin had two sons—the elder called Ebo, the younger called Shenshi; they dwelt in the open forest and could not abide each other; daily they sought shields and spears to attack each other."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 7: Zichan recalled Gaoxin's two sons Ebo and Shenshi, who dwelt in the wildwood, loathed each other, and fought endlessly—the prototype of fraternal strife.

sentences.zh: 注[八]若周公誅管、蔡之類。

translations.literal: Commentary note [eight]: Like the Duke of Zhou executing Guan and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 8: compare the Duke of Zhou's punishment of Guan and Cai.

sentences.zh: 注[九]若齊桓公殺子糾也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [nine]: Like Duke Huan of Qi killing Prince Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 9: as Duke Huan of Qi executed his rival Prince Jiu.

sentences.zh: 昔齊襄公報九世之讎，[一]士□卒荀偃之事，是故春秋美其義，君子稱其信。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xiang of Qi avenged nine generations' revenge; [one] the affair of Shi [lacuna] and Xun Yan—therefore the Spring and Autumn praises its righteousness and gentlemen praise its good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xiang of Qi settled a blood feud nine reigns deep—as in the sequel of Shi Gai (text defective) and Xun Yan—the Spring and Autumn honored the deed and gentlemen praised his steadfast purpose.

sentences.zh: 夫伯游之恨於齊，未若太公之忿於曹也；

translations.literal: Now Bo You's resentment toward Qi does not match the Grand Duke's wrath toward Cao;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yan's vendetta against Qi cannot weigh against your father's rage toward Cao Cao;

sentences.zh: 宣子之臣承業，未若仁君之繼統也。

translations.literal: Xuanzi's ministers continuing the enterprise does not match the humane lord's succession.
translations.idiomatic: nor can Zhao Dun's ministers, carrying forward his work, compare with you who have inherited a humane father's mandate.

sentences.zh: [二] 且君子違難不適讎國，交絕不出惡聲，[三]況忘先人之讎，□親戚之好，而為萬世之戒，遺同盟之恥哉！

translations.literal: [Two] Moreover gentlemen fleeing calamity do not go to an enemy state; when relations are severed they utter no evil sounds—[three] how much more forgetting ancestors' enmity, [lacuna] kinship goodness, and becoming a warning for myriad ages, leaving shame to covenant allies!
translations.idiomatic: [Two] Men of honor who flee peril never shelter with their foes; when friendship ends they leave no bitter words—[three] how then could you cast aside your father's vendetta, break faith with kinsmen, invite everlasting reproach, and shame every ally who stood with you?

sentences.zh: 蠻夷戎狄將有誚讓之言，況我族類，而不痛心邪！

translations.literal: The Man, Yi, Rong, and Di will have words of reproach—how much more we of the same kind—and not ache at heart!
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians on every frontier will sneer at such conduct—how could men of our own stock feel anything but anguish?

sentences.zh: 注[一]公羊傳曰：「紀侯大去其國。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: The Gongyang Commentary says: "Marquis Ji greatly departed his state.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: the Gongyang Commentary asks why "Marquis Ji of Ji abandoned his state in great exodus."

sentences.zh: 大去者何？

translations.literal: What is "greatly departed"?
translations.idiomatic: What does "great departure" signify?

sentences.zh: 滅之也。

translations.literal: It means extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: It means his state was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 孰滅之也？

translations.literal: Who extinguished it?
translations.idiomatic: Who destroyed it?

sentences.zh: 齊滅之。

translations.literal: Qi extinguished it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi did.

sentences.zh: 曷為不言齊滅之？

translations.literal: Why is it not said that Qi extinguished it?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the text not say outright that Qi destroyed Ji?

sentences.zh: 為襄公諱也。

translations.literal: It is to euphemize Duke Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: To shield Duke Xiang from blame.

sentences.zh: 春秋為賢者諱。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn euphemizes for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The classic softens language on behalf of worthy men.

sentences.zh: 何賢於襄公？

translations.literal: In what is Duke Xiang worthy?
translations.idiomatic: What merit earns Duke Xiang such tact?

sentences.zh: 復讎也。

translations.literal: Avenging enmity.
translations.idiomatic: He avenged an ancient wrong.

sentences.zh: 何讎爾？

translations.literal: What enmity?
translations.idiomatic: What grievance?

sentences.zh: 遠祖也。

translations.literal: A remote ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: A wrong done to a remote forebear.

sentences.zh: 哀公烹於周，紀侯譖之。

translations.literal: Duke Ai was boiled at Zhou; Marquis Ji slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai of Qi was boiled alive at the Zhou court because Marquis Ji of Ji slandered him.

sentences.zh: 遠祖者幾代？

translations.literal: The remote ancestor—how many generations?
translations.idiomatic: How many generations lay between them?

sentences.zh: 九代矣。

translations.literal: Nine generations.
translations.idiomatic: Nine reigns.

sentences.zh: 」史記曰，紀侯譖齊哀公於周，周夷王烹哀公。

translations.literal: " The Records says: Marquis Ji slandered Duke Ai of Qi to Zhou; King Yi of Zhou boiled Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The Records record that Marquis Ji maligned Duke Ai of Qi before the Zhou king, and King Yi executed Duke Ai by boiling.

sentences.zh: 其弟靜立，是為胡公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jing was established—this was Duke Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai's brother Jing succeeded him as Duke Hu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 弟獻公立，子武公立，子厲公立，子文公立，子成公立，子莊公立，子厘公立，子襄公八年，紀遷去其邑，是為九代也。

translations.literal: Younger brother Duke Xian was established; son Duke Wu was established; son Duke Li was established; son Duke Wen was established; son Duke Cheng was established; son Duke Zhuang was established; son Duke Xi was established; son—in Duke Xiang's eighth year Ji moved away its settlements—this is nine generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Duke Xian, Duke Wu, Duke Li, Duke Wen, Duke Cheng, Duke Zhuang, Duke Xi, and finally Duke Xiang in whose eighth year Ji abandoned its seat—nine reigns in all.

sentences.zh: 注[二]荀偃，晉大夫也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Xun Yan was a Jin grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Xun Yan served as a Jin minister.

sentences.zh: 左傳曰，荀偃將中軍，士□佐之，伐齊。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: Xun Yan led the central army; Shi [lacuna] assisted him, attacking Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary records that Xun Yan commanded the center army with Shi [character missing in text] as his lieutenant in the attack on Qi.

sentences.zh: 濟河，病目出，及卒，而視不可唅。

translations.literal: They crossed the river; illness made his eyes protrude; when he died his eyes could not be closed for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yellow River his illness bulged his eyes; he died with lids that could not be shut for the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 欒盈曰：「其為未卒事於齊故也？

translations.literal: Luan Ying said: "Could it be because he did not finish the affair in Qi?
translations.idiomatic: Luan Ying asked, "Is it because his business in Qi remained unfinished?"

sentences.zh: 」士□撫之曰：「主苟終，所不嗣事於齊有如河！

translations.literal: " Shi [lacuna] stroked him and said: "If my lord indeed ends, what I would not continue serving Qi—may the Yellow River witness me!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi [character missing in text] pressed his hand on the corpse and swore, "If my lord truly passes from me, may I never again serve Qi—let the Yellow River be my witness!"

sentences.zh: 」乃瞑受含。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he closed his eyes and received the mouth-jade.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could his eyes be closed and the burial jade placed between his teeth.

sentences.zh: 伯游，荀偃字也。

translations.literal: Bo You was Xun Yan's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Bo You was the style of Xun Yan.

sentences.zh: 宣子即士□也，士燮之子，士會之孫。

translations.literal: Xuanzi was Shi [lacuna]—son of Shi Xie, grandson of Shi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: "Xuanzi" is Shi Gai (lacuna in text), son of Shi Xie and grandson of Shi Hui.

sentences.zh: 注[三]左傳曰，公山不狃曰：「君子違難不適讎國。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: The Zuo Commentary says, Gongshan Buniu said: "The gentleman fleeing calamity does not go to an enemy state.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: the Zuo Commentary quotes Gongshan Buniu—"When a gentleman flees disaster he does not seek refuge among enemies."

sentences.zh: 」杜預曰：「違，奔亡也。

translations.literal: " Du Yu says: "Wei means fleeing into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu glosses wei as "to flee for one's life."

sentences.zh: 」史記樂毅遺燕惠王書曰：「臣聞古之君子，交絕不出惡聲。」

translations.literal: " The Records: Yue Yi's letter left to King Hui of Yan says: "I have heard that among gentlemen of old, when friendship is cut off no harsh words are uttered.""
translations.idiomatic: The Records preserves Yue Yi's letter to King Hui of Yan: "Ancient gentlemen, they say, parted without bitter speech."

sentences.zh: 夫欲立竹帛於當時，全宗祀於一世，豈宜同生分謗，爭校得失乎？

translations.literal: Now those who wish to establish themselves on bamboo and silk in their age and preserve ancestral sacrifice for one generation—should they divide slander among those born together and wrangle over gain and loss?
translations.idiomatic: Men who hope to leave a name on the histories and keep their line alive for a generation ought not tear one another apart over petty blame—surely they should not?

sentences.zh: 若冀州有不弟之□，[一]無籩順之節，仁君當降志辱身，以濟事為務。

translations.literal: If Ji province has unfilial younger-brother [lacuna], [one] lacking the ritual order of the feast vessels, the humane lord ought to humble his will and demean his person, taking completing the affair as the task.
translations.idiomatic: Should Ji province prove wanting as a younger brother—lacking the deference shown at the ceremonial mats—the humane lord must swallow pride and bend his knee until the crisis is resolved.

sentences.zh: 事定之後，使天下平其曲直，不亦為高義邪？

translations.literal: After the affair is settled, cause the realm to weigh right and wrong—is this not also lofty righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Once peace returns, let the empire judge who was right—would that not be the nobler course?

sentences.zh: 今仁君見憎於夫人，未若鄭莊之於姜氏；

translations.literal: Now the humane lord is hated by his mother—it does not reach Duke Zhuang of Zheng toward Jiang Shi;
translations.idiomatic: Even if your mother turns against you, the breach cannot rival Duke Zhuang of Zheng and Lady Jiang;

sentences.zh: 昆弟之嫌，未若重華之於象敖。

translations.literal: Suspicion between brothers does not reach Chonghua toward Xiang Ao.
translations.idiomatic: nor can fraternal estrangement exceed what Shun endured from Xiang Ao.

sentences.zh: 然莊公卒崇大隧之樂，像敖終受有鼻之封。

translations.literal: Yet Duke Zhuang finally honored the joy of the great tunnel; Elephant Ao in the end received the enfeoffment of Youbi.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Duke Zhuang found reconciliation in the great tunnel, and Xiang Ao—however cruel—still received the fief at Youbi.

sentences.zh: 願捐□百痾，追攝舊義，復為母子昆弟如初。

translations.literal: Wish to cast aside [lacuna] hundred ailments, pursue and gather old righteousness, again become mother and sons and brothers as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Cast off every old grievance, reclaim the bonds you once shared, and let mothers and sons and brothers be as they were.

sentences.zh: [二]今整勒士馬，瞻望鵠立。

translations.literal: [Two] Now I array horses and men and crane-stand gazing in expectation.
translations.idiomatic: [Two] I have marshaled troops and stand tall as a heron on watch, awaiting your answer.

sentences.zh: 注[一]左傳曰：「段不弟，故不言弟。」

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: The Zuo Commentary says: "Duan was not a proper younger brother; therefore he is not called younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: the Zuo Commentary explains that Duan "was no younger brother," hence the classic withholds the title.

sentences.zh: 注[二]鄭武公娶於申，曰武姜，生莊公及叔段。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Duke Wu of Zheng married from Shen—she was called Wu Jiang—and bore Duke Zhuang and Younger Brother Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Duke Wu of Zheng took a bride from Shen called Wu Jiang; she bore Duke Zhuang and his younger brother Duan.

sentences.zh: 莊公寤生，驚姜氏，遂惡之，愛叔段，欲立之，武公弗許。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang was born feet-first and frightened Jiang Shi; she therefore hated him and loved Younger Brother Duan, wishing to establish him—Duke Wu did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhuang's breech birth frightened Lady Jiang, who came to loathe him while doting on Duan and wishing to make him heir—Duke Wu refused.

sentences.zh: 及莊公立，姜氏為請京，使居之。

translations.literal: When Duke Zhuang was established, Jiang Shi requested Jing for him and caused him to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuang succeeded, Lady Jiang secured the town of Jing for Duan as his seat.

sentences.zh: 段繕甲兵，將襲鄭，夫人將啟之。

translations.literal: Duan repaired armor and weapons, intending to raid Zheng; the lady intended to open the gates for him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan readied arms for a strike on the capital while his mother promised to open the gates.

sentences.zh: 莊公遂寘姜氏於城穎，而誓之曰：「不及黃泉，無相見也。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang thereupon placed Jiang Shi at Chengying and swore to her: "Until we reach the yellow springs, we shall not meet.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang banished his mother to Chengying and swore, "Not until we meet below the yellow springs shall we look upon each other again.

sentences.zh: 」既而悔之。

translations.literal: " Afterwards he regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon repented of his oath.

sentences.zh: 穎考叔曰：「君何患焉？

translations.literal: Ying Kaoshu said: "Why does my lord worry?
translations.idiomatic: Ying Kaoshu asked, "What troubles you, my lord?

sentences.zh: 若闕地及泉，隧而相見，其誰曰不然！

translations.literal: If you dig earth to reach the springs and tunnel to meet—who will say it is not so!
translations.idiomatic: Dig down to the spring line and meet your mother in the tunnel—who will call that breaking your vow?

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " He followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The duke followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 公入而賦：「大隧之中，其樂也融融。

translations.literal: The duke entered and recited: "Within the great tunnel, how joyous and warm.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the tunnel, the duke sang, "Here in the great passage joy flows warm."

sentences.zh: 」姜出而賦：「大隧之外，其樂也洩洩。

translations.literal: " Jiang emerged and recited: "Outside the great tunnel, how joyous and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang answered from without, "Beyond the great passage joy runs free."

sentences.zh: 」遂為母子如初。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they were mother and son as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son were reconciled as before.

sentences.zh: 事見左傳。

translations.literal: The affair is seen in the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: The story appears in the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 史記曰，舜名重華。

translations.literal: The Records says Shun's name was Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: The Records give Shun's second name as Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 父瞽叟盲而舜母死，瞽叟更娶妻，生象。

translations.literal: Father Gusou was blind and Shun's mother died; Gusou again took a wife and bore Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gusou was blind; after Shun's mother died Gusou remarried and fathered Xiang.

sentences.zh: 瞽叟愛後妻子，常欲殺舜。

translations.literal: Gusou loved the children by his later wife and constantly wished to kill Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Gusou doted on his second family and repeatedly tried to murder Shun.

sentences.zh: 舜踐帝位，封弟象為諸侯。

translations.literal: Shun ascended the imperial seat and enfeoffed younger brother Xiang as a feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun took the throne he still ennobled Xiang as a regional lord.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「象至不仁，封諸有鼻。

translations.literal: Mencius says: "Xiang was supremely unkind—he was enfeoffed at Youbi.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius observed that Xiang was utterly devoid of humanity—yet Shun enfeoffed him at Youbi.

sentences.zh: 仁人之於其弟也，不藏怒焉，不宿怨焉，親愛之而已矣。

translations.literal: For the humane man toward his younger brother—he does not harbor anger, does not lodge resentment—he merely loves him, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: A humane ruler feels no lasting wrath toward a brother and bears no overnight grudge—he simply loves him.

sentences.zh: 」鼻國在永州營道縣北，今猶謂之鼻亭。

translations.literal: " The Bi state was north of Yingdao county in Yongzhou; today it is still called Bi pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The polity of Bi lay north of Yingdao in Yongzhou—locals still call the site Bi Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 又與尚書諫之，並不從。

translations.literal: Again he remonstrated with the Secretariat—both did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the same course through the Secretariat as well; neither memorial swayed them.

sentences.zh: [一] 注[一]《魏氏春秋》載表遺尚書曰：「知變起辛、郭，禍結同生，追閼伯、實沈之蹤，忘常棣死喪之義，親尋干戈，殭屍流血，聞之哽咽，若存若亡。

translations.literal: [One] Commentary note [one]: Annals of Wei records Biao's letter left to the Secretariat: "Knowing trouble arose from Xin and Guo, disaster bound between those born together, following the tracks of Ebo and Shenshi, forgetting the cherry-blossom brothers' meaning for death and mourning, personally seeking shields and spears, stiff corpses flowing blood—hearing it chokes the throat, as if alive as if dead.
translations.idiomatic: [One] Commentary, note 1: the Annals of Wei preserves Liu Biao's memorial to the Secretariat: "You know the quarrel sprang from Xin Ping and Guo Tu, that womb-mates have tied disaster upon themselves, that they tread the path of Ebo and Shenshi and forget the cherry-tree ode's lesson on mourning kin—that brothers take up arms themselves and corpses litter the field. The tale sticks in my throat; I scarce know whether I breathe or no."

sentences.zh: 昔軒轅有涿鹿之戰，周公有商、奄之師，皆所以翦除穢害而定王業，非強弱之爭，喜怒之忿也。

translations.literal: Formerly Xuanyuan fought at Zhuolu; the Duke of Zhou led campaigns against Shang and Yan—all were means to cut away corruption and anchor legitimate kingship, not mere contests of strength or fits of temper.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor fought at Zhuolu; the Duke of Zhou campaigned against Shang and Yan—all to purge wickedness and secure the kingship, not schoolyard quarrels born of pique.

sentences.zh: 故雖滅親不尤，誅兄不傷。

translations.literal: Therefore although destroying kin is not blame, executing elder brother does not wound.
translations.idiomatic: Hence extirpating kin draws no reproach when duty demands it, and striking down an elder brother need not rend the heart when justice requires it.

sentences.zh: 今二君初承洪業，纂繼前軌，進有國家傾危之慮，退有先公遺恨之負。

translations.literal: Now the two lords first inherit the great enterprise, continue the former track—advancing they have concern for state overturning peril, retreating they bear the late lord's leftover hatred.
translations.idiomatic: You two have barely mounted your father's enterprise: advance, and the dynasty totters; fall back, and your father's vendetta goes unavenged.

sentences.zh: 當唯曹是務，唯國是康。

translations.literal: They ought to take only Cao as task, only the state as peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your sole business must be Cao Cao; your sole aim the realm's safety.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 金木水火剛柔相濟，然後克得其和，能為人用。

translations.literal: Metal, wood, water, fire—hard and soft mutually aid—then they can obtain harmony and be used by men.
translations.idiomatic: Metal, wood, water, and fire need hard and soft in balance before they harmonize and serve human ends.

sentences.zh: 今青州天性峭急，迷於曲直。

translations.literal: Now Qingzhou by nature is precipitate and hasty, confused about crooked and straight.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou is rash by temperament and blind to who is right.

sentences.zh: 仁君度數弘廣，綽然有餘，當以大苞小，以優容劣，先除曹操，以平先公之恨，事定之後，乃議曲直之評，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: The humane lord's measures are vast and broad, abundantly more than enough—ought to use large to embrace small, use surplus to tolerate inferior, first eliminate Cao Cao to settle the late lord's hatred; after the affair is settled, then discuss judging right and wrong—is this not good!
translations.idiomatic: You, my lord, are generous and far-sighted: shelter the lesser brother with the greater, indulge fault with merit. Destroy Cao Cao first to satisfy your father's ghost; once peace holds, let the world debate who was wrong—could any course be wiser?

sentences.zh: 若留神遠圖，克己復禮，當振旅長驅，共□王室。

translations.literal: If attending to far plans, restraining self and restoring ritual, ought to rouse the army and drive long, together [lacuna] the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: If you think ahead, master yourselves, and return to ritual, raise your hosts and ride hard to aid the house of Han together.

sentences.zh: 若迷而不返，遵而無改，則胡夷將有誚讓之言，況我同盟，復能戮力仁君之役哉！

translations.literal: If lost and not returning, following without changing—then Hu and Yi will have reproaching words; how much more we covenant allies—again able to join strength to the humane lord's campaign!
translations.idiomatic: If you stay lost, cling to error, and refuse reform, even barbarians will mock you—how could your allies ever again march for you?

sentences.zh: 此韓盧、東郭自困於前，而遺田父之獲者也。

translations.literal: This is Han Lu and Dongguo trapping themselves in front and leaving the field farmer's catch.
translations.idiomatic: You would become the hound Han Lu and the hare of Dongguo—exhausting each other until some peasant bags you both.

sentences.zh: 憤躍鶴望，冀聞和同之聲。

translations.literal: Angry leap, crane-gazing—hope to hear harmony's sound.
translations.idiomatic: I pace like a crane on watch, desperate for word that you have made peace.

sentences.zh: 若其泰也，則袁族其與漢升降乎！

translations.literal: If it goes smoothly—then the Yuan clan perhaps with Han rises and falls!
translations.idiomatic: If matters mend, the Yuan may yet rise and fall with the house of Han.

sentences.zh: 如其否也，則同盟永無望矣。

translations.literal: If it is not so—then covenant allies forever without hope.
translations.idiomatic: If not, your allies will never again place hope in you.

sentences.zh: 」表二書並見王粲集。

translations.literal: " Both Biao's letters are seen in Wang Can's collection.
translations.idiomatic: Both of Liu Biao's letters are preserved in Wang Can's literary collection.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，尚使審配守鄴，復攻譚於平原。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year Shang sent Shen Pei to guard Ye and again attacked Tan in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year of the Jian'an era, Yuan Shang left Shen Pei to hold Ye and again struck Yuan Tan in Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 配獻書於譚曰：「配聞良藥苦口而利於病，忠言逆耳而便於行。

translations.literal: Pei presented a letter to Tan: "Pei has heard good medicine is bitter in the mouth but benefits illness; loyal words offend the ear but ease action.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei wrote to Yuan Tan: "They say effective physic tastes foul yet cures the sick; honest counsel grates the ear yet keeps one upright.

sentences.zh: [一]願將軍緩心抑怒，終省愚辭。

translations.literal: [One] Wish the general slow heart and suppress anger, finally examine foolish words.
translations.idiomatic: [One] I beg you to calm your heart, master your wrath, and hear me through.

sentences.zh: 蓋春秋之義，國君死社稷，忠臣死君命。

translations.literal: As for the Spring and Autumn's meaning—the state lord dies for altars of soil and grain; loyal ministers die for lordly command.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn teaches that rulers die with their altars and ministers die carrying out their orders.

sentences.zh: [二]苟圖危宗廟，剝亂國家，親□一也。

translations.literal: [Two] If plotting to endanger the ancestral temple, stripping and disordering the state—kinship [lacuna] is one.
translations.idiomatic: [Two] Whoever would imperil the shrines and rip the realm apart—kinsman or outsider—is alike condemned.

sentences.zh: [三]是以周公垂涕以*

translations.literal: [Three] Therefore the Duke of Zhou shed tears as he executed Guan and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: [Three] That is why the Duke of Zhou wept even as he dealt with Guan and Cai.

translations.literal: (execute)
translations.idiomatic: (execute)

sentences.zh: **[蔽]*管、蔡之獄，[四]季友歔欷而行叔牙之誅。

translations.literal: **[variant graph]* the cases of Guan and Cai; [four] Jiyou sobbed through his nose while carrying out Shuya's execution.
translations.idiomatic: **—resolved the trials of Guan and Cai; [four] Jiyou wept aloud when he executed Shuya.

sentences.zh: [五]何則？

translations.literal: [Five] Why?
translations.idiomatic: [Five] Why?

sentences.zh: 義重人輕，事不獲已故也。

translations.literal: Righteousness heavy, persons light—the affair could not be helped, therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Duty outweighs affection when no other course remains.

sentences.zh: 昔先公廢黜將軍以續賢兄，立我將軍以為嫡嗣，上告祖靈，下書譜牒，海內遠近，誰不備聞！

translations.literal: Formerly the late lord demoted the general to continue the worthy elder brother, established our general as heir apparent, reported above to ancestral spirits, inscribed below in genealogy registers—within the seas far and near, who has not fully heard!
translations.idiomatic: Your father set you aside for your worthy elder brother, raised our lord as heir, announced it to the ancestors, entered it in the clan register—the whole empire knows it.

sentences.zh: 何意凶臣郭圖，妄畫蛇足，[六]曲辭諂媚，交亂懿親。

translations.literal: Who would have thought evil minister Guo Tu vainly drew snake feet; [six] crooked words flattery, mutually disordering august kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet villain Guo Tu added feet to the snake—[six] twisted flattery that set noble brothers at war.

sentences.zh: 至令將軍忘孝友之仁，襲閼、沉之多，放兵鈔突，屠城殺吏，冤魂痛於幽冥，創痍被於草棘。

translations.literal: Extending to causing the general to forget benevolence of filiality and friendship, repeat the crimes of Ebo and Shenshi in excess, unleash troops on raids, slaughter cities and kill clerks—wronged souls ache in the dark realm, wounds spread over grass and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: He made you forget every duty of son and brother, pile outrage upon the feud of Ebo and Shenshi, rampage with arms, sack cities, and butcher officials—the dead groan in the shades and the wounded litter the moors.

sentences.zh: 又乃圖獲鄴城，許賞賜秦胡，其財物婦女，豫有分數。

translations.literal: Moreover then plotting to seize Ye city, promising rewards to Qin and Hu soldiery—those goods and women had predetermined portions.
translations.idiomatic: You plotted to seize Ye and promised plunder to frontier troops—every coin and captive already counted out.

sentences.zh: 又云：『孤雖有老母，趣使身體完具而已。

translations.literal: Also saying: "Although I have an old mother, urge only that her body be kept whole, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: You even said, "I still have an aged mother—only keep her alive; that is enough for me."

sentences.zh: 』聞此言者，莫不悼心揮涕，使太夫人憂哀憤隔，我州君臣監寐悲歎。

translations.literal: " Those who heard these words none failed to mourn heart and wipe tears—causing the grand lady sorrow grief rage separation—our province lord and ministers watched sleep mourning sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard it wept blood for pity—your mother heartsick with rage and grief, every officer in Ji awake nights groaning.

sentences.zh: 誠拱默以聽執事之圖，則懼違春秋死命之節，詒太夫人不測之患，損先公不世之業。

translations.literal: If truly folding hands silent to listen to the steward's plans—then fear violating Spring and Autumn die-for-command integrity, leave the grand lady unforeseen calamity, harm the late lord's unequaled enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Were we to fold our hands and obey your schemes, we would betray the Spring and Autumn ideal of dying for duty, bring unspeakable sorrow on your mother, and wreck your father's incomparable legacy.

sentences.zh: 我將軍辭不獲命，以及館陶之役。

translations.literal: Our general declining did not obtain consent—thereupon to the Guantao campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord could not decline his orders forever—hence the battle at Guantao.

sentences.zh: [七]伏惟將軍至孝蒸蒸，發於岐嶷，友於之性，生於自然，章之以聰明，行之以敏達，覽古今之舉措，鶯興敗之征符，輕榮財於糞土，貴名*

translations.literal: [Seven] I reflect that the general's supreme filial steam issued from childhood precocity; the nature of friendship toward brothers was born from what is natural; manifest through cleverness, enacted through quick penetration; viewing ancient and modern measures, discerning omens of rise and fall; treating glory and wealth lightly as dung soil; honoring name—
translations.idiomatic: [Seven] You were famed for filial devotion from boyhood, gentle toward brothers by native temper, sharpened by wit, versed in history's precedents, alert to omens of fortune—wealth you counted as dust and reputation you prized—

translations.literal: (high)
translations.idiomatic: (high)

sentences.zh: **[位]*於丘岳。

translations.literal: **[position]* higher than hills and peaks.
translations.idiomatic: **—higher than mountain peaks.

sentences.zh: 何意奄然迷沉，墮賢哲之操，[八]積怨肆忿，取破家之禍！

translations.literal: Who would have thought suddenly lost sunken, falling from worthy wise conduct—[eight] piling resentment unleashing anger, incurring destroy-house calamity!
translations.idiomatic: Who could dream you would sink into folly, betray every noble resolve—[eight] nurse grudge on grudge, and court the ruin of your house?

sentences.zh: 翹企延頸，待望讎敵，委慈親於虎狼之牙，以逞一朝之志，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Crane-stand crane-neck, waiting gazing at foe enemies, abandoning kindly parent to tiger-wolf teeth, to display one morning's ambition—is it not painful!
translations.idiomatic: You crane your neck toward enemies while laying your gentle mother between wolves' jaws to gratify a moment's whim—could any sight wound us more?

sentences.zh: 若乃天啟尊心，革圖易慮，則我將軍匍匐悲號於將軍股掌之上，配等亦當□躬布體以聽斧鍎之刑。

translations.literal: If then Heaven opens your heart, changing your plan and thought—then our general will crawl, sob, and wail in the palm of your hand; I, Pei, and my colleagues will likewise [lacuna] our persons to accept the headsman's blade.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven moves you to abandon this war, our lord will weep at your feet and I will stretch out my neck for the executioner.

sentences.zh: 如又不悛，禍將及之。

translations.literal: If again not reforming, calamity will reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse again and ruin will overtake you.

sentences.zh: 願熟詳吉凶，以賜環玦。

translations.literal: Wish maturely examine good and ill, to grant ring or jade half-disk.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh fortune against disaster and send back ring or broken jade—your answer.

sentences.zh: 」[九]譚不納。

translations.literal: " [Nine] Tan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " [Nine] Yuan Tan spurned the letter.

sentences.zh: 注[一]孔子家語曰：「忠言逆耳而利於行。」

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Confucius's School Sayings says: "Loyal words offend the ear but benefit action."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: the School Sayings records Confucius on blunt counsel that profits conduct.

sentences.zh: 注[二]左傳晏嬰曰：「君為社稷死則死之，為社稷亡則亡之。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Yan Ying in the Zuo Commentary says: "If the lord dies for altars of soil and grain then die for him; if he flees for altars of soil and grain then flee for him.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Yan Ying taught that ministers share their lord's death or exile when the altars are at stake.

sentences.zh: 」又晉解楊曰：「受命以出，有死無隕。

translations.literal: " Further Jin's Xie Yang says: "Receiving orders and going forth—there is death but no falling.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yang of Jin vowed that once commissioned abroad one might die but never fail.

sentences.zh: 死而成命，臣之祿也。」

translations.literal: Death and accomplishing command—this is the minister's emolument.""
translations.idiomatic: To die fulfilling one's charge is a minister's reward."

sentences.zh: 注[三]左傳曰「天實剝亂」也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: The Zuo Commentary says "Heaven indeed strips and disorders".
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: the Zuo Commentary blames Heaven for "ravaging good order."

sentences.zh: 注[四]左傳曰，鄭子太叔曰：「周公殺管叔，放蔡叔。

translations.literal: Commentary note [four]: The Zuo Commentary says, Zitaishu of Zheng says: "The Duke of Zhou killed Guan Shu and banished Cai Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 4: Zitaishu of Zheng recalled how the Duke of Zhou executed Guan Shu and exiled Cai Shu.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不愛？

translations.literal: How could he not love?
translations.idiomatic: Was it for lack of love?

sentences.zh: 王室故也。」

translations.literal: It was for the royal house's sake.""
translations.idiomatic: No—for the sake of the royal house."

sentences.zh: 注[五]公羊傳曰：「公子牙卒。

translations.literal: Commentary note [five]: The Gongyang Commentary says: "Young lord Ya died.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 5: the Gongyang Commentary records that "Young lord Ya died."

sentences.zh: 何以不稱弟？

translations.literal: Why is he not called younger brother?
translations.idiomatic: Why not style him "younger brother"?

sentences.zh: 殺也，為季子諱殺也。

translations.literal: He was killed—to euphemize killing for Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was executed—the classic softens the blow for Jizi's sake.

sentences.zh: 莊公病，叔牙曰：『魯一生一及，君以知之。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang was ill; Shuya said: "Lu has one generation rising and one reaching—you know it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Zhuang lay dying, Shuya reminded him, "Lu allows succession once by birth and once by seniority—you know the rule.

sentences.zh: 慶父存也。

translations.literal: Qingfu survives.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu still lives.

sentences.zh: 』季子曰：『夫何敢？

translations.literal: " Jizi said: "How would I dare?
translations.idiomatic: Jizi answered, "How could I presume?

sentences.zh: 是將為亂！

translations.literal: This will become rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: That path leads to rebellion!

sentences.zh: 』和藥而飲之，曰：『公子從吾言而飲此，則可以無為天下戮笑，必有後於魯國。

translations.literal: " He blended medicine and gave him to drink, saying: "Young lord, if you follow my words and drink this, then you can avoid being mocked by the realm and will surely have posterity in Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He mixed poison and said, "Drink this for my sake and you spare Lu worldwide ridicule and leave heirs.

sentences.zh: 』誅不避兄弟，君臣之義也。」

translations.literal: " Punishment does not avoid brothers—it is the meaning of lord and minister.""
translations.idiomatic: " Execution cannot spare brothers when duty demands—that is the covenant between lord and servant."

sentences.zh: 注[六]戰國策曰：「楚有祠者，賜其舍人酒一琶，相謂曰：『數人飲之不足，一人飲之有餘，請各畫地為蛇，先成者飲酒。

translations.literal: Commentary note [six]: Intrigues of the Warring States says: "Chu had one who sacrificed and granted his retainers one hu of wine; they said to each other: "Several drinking it is not enough; one drinking it has surplus—please each draw a snake on the ground; whoever finishes first drinks the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 6: the Intrigues tell of Chu retainers given one flask of sacrificial wine; unable to share it fairly they agreed to draw snakes on the ground—the fastest hand would drink.

sentences.zh: 』一人蛇先成，引酒且飲，乃左手持酒，右手畫蛇，曰：『吾能為之足。

translations.literal: " One man's snake was finished first; he drew the wine and was about to drink; then left hand held wine, right hand drew snake, saying: "I can give it feet.
translations.idiomatic: One man finished first and reached for the cup—then added feet to his snake with his free hand, boasting, "I can give it legs.

sentences.zh: 』未成，一人蛇成，奪其琶，曰：『蛇固無足，子安能為足？

translations.literal: " Not yet finished; another man's snake finished—seized his hu, saying: "Snakes fundamentally lack feet—how can you give feet?
translations.idiomatic: Before he drank, a rival finished and snatched the flask: "Snakes have no feet—what fool draws legs on them?

sentences.zh: 』遂飲酒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he drank the wine.
translations.idiomatic: So he drank the wine.

sentences.zh: 為蛇足者終亡其酒。」

translations.literal: He who added snake feet in the end lost his wine."
translations.idiomatic: The man who drew feet on his snake forfeited the cup in the end."

sentences.zh: 注[七]詒，遺也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [seven]: Yi means leave behind.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 7: yi here means "to bequeath" or "to inflict upon."

sentences.zh: 不世猶言非常也。

translations.literal: "Unequaled in generations" is like saying extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: "Unequaled for generations" simply means extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 獻帝春秋曰：「譚尚遂尋干戈，以相征討。

translations.literal: Annals of Emperor Xian says: "Tan and Shang thereupon sought shields and spears, attacking each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian relate that Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang took up arms and marched against each other.

sentences.zh: 譚軍不利，保於平原，尚乃軍於館陶。

translations.literal: Tan army was not favorable—secured at Pingyuan; Shang then encamped at Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan faltered and held Pingyuan while Yuan Shang camped at Guantao.

sentences.zh: 譚擊之敗，尚走保險。

translations.literal: Tan attacked him and was defeated; Shang fled and secured defiles.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan attacked and lost; Yuan Shang withdrew into strong ground.

sentences.zh: 譚追攻之，尚設奇伏大破譚軍，殭屍流血不可勝計。

translations.literal: Tan pursued and attacked him; Shang set strange ambushes and greatly defeated Tan's army—stiff corpses flowing blood beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Tan pressed the pursuit, Yuan Shang laid an ambush and shattered his army—dead beyond counting littered the field.

sentences.zh: 譚走還平原。」

translations.literal: Tan fled back to Pingyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan fled once more to Pingyuan."

sentences.zh: 注[八]墮音許規反。

translations.literal: Commentary note [eight]: Duo is read xu gui fan.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 8: duo is pronounced like xu gui (falling tone).

sentences.zh: 注[九]《孫卿子》曰：「絕人以玦，反人以環。」

translations.literal: Commentary note [nine]: Sun Qingzi says: "Break with someone using a jade half-disk; return someone using a ring."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 9: Xun Qing taught that one sends a broken jade disk to refuse alliance and a ring to invite return.

sentences.zh: 曹操因此進攻鄴，審配將馮*

translations.literal: Cao Cao therefore advanced to attack Ye; Shen Pei led Feng—
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pressed the siege of Ye; Shen Pei's officer Feng

translations.idiomatic: (Zha)

sentences.zh: **[禮]*為內應，開突門內操兵三百餘人。

translations.literal: **[Li]* as inner responder, opened the sally-port and admitted more than three hundred of Cao's troops.
translations.idiomatic: **—styled Li—was to open the sally gate from within and admit three hundred of Cao's men.

sentences.zh: [一] 配覺之，從城上以大石擊門，門閉，入者皆死。

translations.literal: [One] Pei perceived it; from atop the wall used a great stone to strike the gate—the gate closed; those who entered all died.
translations.idiomatic: [One] Shen Pei uncovered the plot and hurled a boulder from the wall onto the gate; it slammed shut and trapped every infiltrator inside.

sentences.zh: 操乃鑿燎圍城，周回四十里，初令淺，示若可越。

translations.literal: Cao thereupon dug moats encircling the city—forty li round—at first ordering them shallow, showing as if passable.
translations.idiomatic: Cao threw up a forty-li trench works around Ye, keeping the ditch shallow at first so the defenders might think it fordable.

sentences.zh: 配望見，笑而不出爭利。

translations.literal: Pei looked and saw—laughed and did not come out to contest advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei watched and laughed, refusing to sortie for a cheap gain.

sentences.zh: 操一夜浚之，廣深二丈，引漳水以灌之。

translations.literal: Cao in one night dredged them—two ren wide and deep—led Zhang River water to inundate them.
translations.idiomatic: In one night Cao deepened the trench two ren and diverted the Zhang River to flood it.

sentences.zh: 自五月至八月，城中餓死者過半。

translations.literal: From the fifth month to the eighth month, within the city those dead from hunger exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: Between the fifth and eighth months more than half the population starved inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 尚聞鄴急，將軍萬餘人還救城，操逆擊破之。

translations.literal: Shang heard Ye was urgent—led more than ten thousand troops back to rescue the city; Cao met attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shang heard Ye's peril he marched back with ten thousand men; Cao intercepted and routed him.

sentences.zh: 尚走依曲漳為營，[二]操復圍之，未合，尚懼，遣陰夔、陳琳求降，不聽。

translations.literal: Tan fled relying on winding Zhang to make camp; [two] Cao again surrounded him—not yet closed—Shang feared and sent Yin Kui and Chen Lin to seek surrender—not listened.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang fell back along the Zhang's bend to camp; [two] Cao caught him before the encirclement closed. Yuan Shang panicked and sent Yin Kui and Chen Lin to sue for peace—Cao refused.

sentences.zh: 尚還走藍口，[三]操復進，急圍之。

translations.literal: Shang further fled to Lankou; [three] Cao again advanced and urgently surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: He fled again toward Lankou; [three] Cao pressed forward and tightened the cordon.

sentences.zh: 尚將馬延等臨陣降，觿大潰，尚奔中山。

translations.literal: Shang's generals Ma Yan and others faced battle and surrendered—the army greatly routed; Shang fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: General Ma Yan and others capitulated on the field; the Yuan army collapsed and Yuan Shang bolted for Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 盡收其輜重，得尚印綬節鉞及衣物，以示城中，城中崩沮。

translations.literal: All seized his baggage train—obtained Shang's seals, cords, tally-axe, and clothing—to show the city—within the city collapsed and despondent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao captured the baggage train, Shang's seals, baton, and wardrobe, and paraded them before Ye until morale inside crumbled.

sentences.zh: 審配令士卒曰：「堅守死戰，操軍疲矣。

translations.literal: Pei ordered soldiers saying: "Firmly defend and fight to death—Cao's army is weary.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei told his men, "Hold fast and fight to the death—Cao's troops are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 幽州方至，何憂無主！

translations.literal: Youzhou is just arriving—why worry about lacking a lord!
translations.idiomatic: Relief from Youzhou is almost here—why fear we lack a leader?

sentences.zh: 」操出行圍，配伏弩射之，幾中。

translations.literal: " Cao went out to inspect the siege lines—Pei laid crossbows and shot him—almost hit.
translations.idiomatic: " When Cao rode the lines to inspect them, Shen Pei's hidden crossbows nearly struck him.

sentences.zh: [四]以其兄子榮為東門校尉，榮夜開門內操兵，配拒戰城中，生獲配。

translations.literal: [Four] Using his elder brother's son Rong as eastern gate colonel—Rong opened the gate by night admitting Cao troops—Pei resisted fighting within the city—alive captured Pei.
translations.idiomatic: [Four] Shen Pei had appointed his nephew Shen Rong captain of the east gate; Rong opened it by night for Cao's men. Shen Pei fought street by street until taken alive.

sentences.zh: 操謂配曰：「吾近行圍，弩何多也？

translations.literal: Cao said to Pei: "When I lately toured the siege lines—why so many crossbows?
translations.idiomatic: Cao asked Shen Pei, "When I rode the perimeter the other day, why were there so many bolts aimed at me?

sentences.zh: 」配曰：「猶恨其少。

translations.literal: " Pei said: "Still hate they were few.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei replied, "I only regret there were not more."

sentences.zh: 」操曰：「卿忠於袁氏，亦自不得不爾。

translations.literal: " Cao said: "You are loyal to the Yuan clan—itself must be thus.
translations.idiomatic: Cao said, "Your loyalty to the Yuans forced your hand—I understand."

sentences.zh: 」意欲活之。

translations.literal: " His intention wished to keep him alive.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to spare him.

sentences.zh: 配意氣壯烈，終無撓辭，見者莫不歎息，遂斬之。

translations.literal: Pei's bearing was heroic and fierce—finally had no yielding words—those who saw none failed not to sigh—thereupon executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei faced death unbowed; every witness sighed, yet Cao ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: [五]全尚母妻子，還其財寶。

translations.literal: [Five] Preserved Shang's mother, wife, and children—returned his treasures.
translations.idiomatic: [Five] Cao spared Yuan Shang's mother, wives, and children and restored his goods.

sentences.zh: 高干以并州降，復為刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Gan with Bingzhou surrendered—again became inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan surrendered Bing province and was reappointed inspector.

sentences.zh: 注[一]《墨子·備突篇》曰「城百步，一突門。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Mozi's "Preparing Sally-Ports" chapter says "City hundred bu—one sally-port.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Mozi's chapter on sally ports prescribes one gate every hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 突門用車兩輪，以木朿之塗其上，維置突門內。

translations.literal: Sally-port uses cart two wheels—wood binds them and mud coats above—tie place inside sally-port.
translations.idiomatic: Block the tunnel with two cart wheels bound in timber and mud, then suspend them inside the sally gate.

sentences.zh: 度門廣狹之，令人入門四尺，中置窐突，門旁為橐，充醋狀，又置艾。

translations.literal: Measure gate wide narrow—cause men enter gate four chi—middle place recessed tunnel—gate side make bellows—fill vinegar appearance—also place mugwort.
translations.idiomatic: Gauge the gateway's width: let attackers advance four chi inside, sink a pit trap mid-passage, mount bellows along the wall shaped like vinegar jars, and heap mugwort.

sentences.zh: 寇即入，下輪而塞之，鼓橐熏之」也。

translations.literal: When raiders enter—lower wheels and block them—beat bellows and smoke them"—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders pour in, drop the wheels to seal the tunnel and pump smoke through the bellows."

sentences.zh: 注[二]漳水之曲。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: The Zhang River's bend.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: a bend of the Zhang River.

translations.idiomatic: **—yang—county contains Mount Lancuo near Ye—the mouth of Blue Mountain.

translations.literal: Commentary note [four]: Ji is read qi.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 4: ji here rhymes with qi.
