translations.literal: Zhong is read zhu zhong fan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong is read with the bamboo initial and departing tone.

sentences.zh: 注[五]先賢行狀曰：「是日先縛配將詣帳下，辛毗等逆以馬鞭擊其頭，罵之曰：『奴，汝今日真死矣。

translations.literal: Commentary note [five]: Conduct of Former Worthies says: "That day first bound Pei general brought to tent below—Xin Pi and others met using horse whip struck his head, reviling saying: 'Slave—you today truly die.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 5: Conduct of Former Worthies records that Shen Pei was bound first and dragged to headquarters; Xin Pi and others met him with riding crops across the face, shouting, "Dog—you die today for certain."

sentences.zh: 』配顧曰：『狗輩！

translations.literal: " Pei looked back saying: 'Dog pack!
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei shot back, "Cur!"

sentences.zh: 由汝曹破冀州，恨不得殺汝。

translations.literal: Because you crowd destroyed Ji province—hate not obtaining killing you.
translations.idiomatic: You rats wrecked Ji—I only regret I cannot kill you myself.

sentences.zh: 』太祖既有意活配，配無撓辭，辛毗等號哭不已，乃殺之。」

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor already had intention to keep Pei alive—Pei had no yielding words—Xin Pi and others wailed without cease—thereupon killed him."
translations.idiomatic: Though Cao wished to spare him, Shen Pei would not bend; Xin Pi and his kin howled without end until Cao ordered his death."

sentences.zh: 曹操之圍鄴也，譚復背之，因略取甘陵、安平、勃海、河閒，攻尚於中山。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao besieged Ye, Tan again betrayed him—thereupon raided and took Ganling, Anping, Bohai, Hejian—attacked Shang at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao besieged Ye, Yuan Tan broke faith again, seized Ganling, Anping, Bohai, and Hejian, and struck Yuan Shang at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 尚敗，走故安從熙，而譚悉收其觿，還屯龍湊。

translations.literal: Shang defeated—fled Gu'an joining Xi—while Tan all seized his army—returned encamped Longcou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang lost and fled to Gu'an to join Yuan Xi; Yuan Tan swallowed his army whole and pulled back to Longcou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，曹操討譚，軍其門。

translations.literal: Twelfth month—Cao Cao punished Tan—armied at his gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Cao Cao marched against Yuan Tan and camped at his gates.

sentences.zh: 譚夜遁*

translations.literal: Tan fled by night—
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan slipped away by night—

translations.literal: (run)
translations.idiomatic: (flee)

sentences.zh: **[走]*南皮，臨清河而屯。

translations.literal: **[zou]* Nanpi—faced Qing River and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: **—to Nanpi—where he camped along the Qing River.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，急攻之。

translations.literal: Next year first month—urgently attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year's first month saw furious assaults.

sentences.zh: 譚欲出戰，軍未合而破。

translations.literal: Tan wished to exit battle—army not yet joined and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan tried to sortie before his lines closed and was shattered.

sentences.zh: 譚被發驅馳，追者意非恆人，趨奔之。

translations.literal: Tan loosed hair galloping—pursuers thought him not ordinary person—rushed running him.
translations.idiomatic: With hair streaming he fled so wildly his pursuers mistook him for someone extraordinary and raced after him.

sentences.zh: [一] 譚墯馬，顧曰：「咄，兒過我，我能富貴汝。

translations.literal: [One] Tan fell from horse—looked back saying: "Tut—boy pass me—I can enrich honor you.
translations.idiomatic: [One] Yuan Tan was thrown from his saddle and cried to the soldier who overtook him, "Boy—let me pass and I will make your fortune.

sentences.zh: 」言未絕口，頭已斷地。

translations.literal: " Words not yet cut off—head already severed on ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking his head rolled in the dust.

sentences.zh: 於是斬郭圖等，戮其妻子。

translations.literal: Thereupon executed Guo Tu and others—executed their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tu and his faction were beheaded and their families slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 注[一]趨音促。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Qu is read cu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: qu here is read cu (urgent).

sentences.zh: 熙、尚為其將焦觸、張南所攻，奔遼西烏桓。

translations.literal: Xi and Shang were attacked by their generals Jiao Chu and Zhang Nan—fled to Liaoxi Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi and Yuan Shang were attacked by their own officers Jiao Chu and Zhang Nan and fled to the Wuhuan of western Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 觸自號幽州刺史，驅率諸郡太守令長背袁向曹，陳兵數萬。

translations.literal: Chu styled himself Youzhou Inspector—drove and led various commandery prefects magistrates turning back from Yuan toward Cao—arrayed troops several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Chu proclaimed himself inspector of Youzhou, pressed every county magistrate to abandon the Yuans for Cao, and marshaled tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 殺白馬盟，令曰：「違者斬！

translations.literal: Slaughtered white horse covenant—ordered saying: "Violators beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: They slew a white horse for covenant wine and proclaimed, "Whoever breaks this oath dies!

sentences.zh: 」觿莫敢仰視，各以次歃。

translations.literal: " Army none dared look up—each in order sipped.
translations.idiomatic: No soldier dared lift his eyes; one by one they tasted the blood.

sentences.zh: 至別駕代郡韓珩，[一]曰：「吾受袁公父子厚恩，今其破亡，智不能救，勇不能死，於義闕矣。

translations.literal: When reached Adjutant Administrator Dai commandery Han Heng—[one] said: "I received Duke Yuan father and son thick kindness—now their destruction—I wisdom cannot rescue—courage cannot die—for righteousness lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When the cup reached Adjutant Administrator Han Heng of Dai, [one] he declared, "The Yuans heaped kindness on me; now they lie broken and I lack wit to save them or courage to die with them—I fail every duty.

sentences.zh: 若乃北面曹氏，所不能為也！

translations.literal: As for turning north face Cao clan—that which cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: As for kneeling to Cao—that I cannot do!

sentences.zh: 」一坐為珩失色。

translations.literal: " Whole seating for Heng lost color.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly blanched.

sentences.zh: 觸曰：「夫舉大事，當立大義。

translations.literal: Chu said: "Now raising great affair—ought establish great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Chu replied, "Great ventures rest on great principle.

sentences.zh: 事之濟否，不待一人，可卒珩志，以厲事君。

translations.literal: Affair's success or not—not waiting one person—can fulfill Heng's intent—to encourage serving lord.
translations.idiomatic: Whether we succeed does not hinge on one man; honor Han Heng's resolve and stiffen loyalty everywhere.

sentences.zh: 」[二]曹操聞珩節，甚高之，屢辟不至，卒於家。

translations.literal: " [Two] Cao Cao heard Heng's integrity—greatly esteemed him—repeatedly summoned did not arrive—died at home.
translations.idiomatic: " [Two] Cao Cao admired Han Heng's integrity and summoned him repeatedly; Han never came and died at home.

sentences.zh: 注[一]珩音行。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Heng is read hang.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: heng is pronounced like hang.

sentences.zh: 注[二]先賢行狀曰「珩字子佩，代郡人，清粹有雅量。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Conduct of Former Worthies says "Heng styled Zip—Dai commandery man—pure refined having generous capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Conduct of Former Worthies calls Han Heng Zip of Dai—pure in character and broad of temper.

sentences.zh: 少喪父母，奉養兄姊，宗族稱悌」也。

translations.literal: Young lost parents—served elder brothers sisters—clan praised fraternal submission"—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he cared for elder siblings and earned the clan's praise for fraternal devotion."

sentences.zh: 高干復叛，執上黨太守，舉兵守壺口關。

translations.literal: Gao Gan again rebelled—seized Shangdang prefect—raised troops guarding Hukou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan rebelled again, seized the governor of Shangdang, and held Hukou Pass.

sentences.zh: [一]十一年，曹操自征干，干乃留其將守城，自詣匈奴求救，不得，獨與數騎亡，欲南奔荊州。

translations.literal: [One] Eleventh year—Cao Cao personally campaigned Gan—Gan thereupon left his general guard city—himself went to Xiongnu seeking rescue—not obtained—alone with several riders fled—wished south flee Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [One] In the eleventh year Cao Cao marched against Gao Gan in person. Gan left a deputy to hold the city and rode to the Xiongnu for aid; refused, he fled south toward Jingzhou with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 上洛都尉捕斬之。

translations.literal: Shangluo commandant captured executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant of Shangluo ran him down and struck off his head.

sentences.zh: [二] 注[一]潞州上黨縣有壺山口，因其險而置關焉。

translations.literal: [Two] Commentary note [one]: Luzhou Shangdang county has Hukou mountain mouth—because its peril established pass there.
translations.idiomatic: [Two] Commentary, note 1: Hukou Pass sits on the narrows of Mount Hu in Shangdang county of Lu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 注[二]典論曰：「上洛都尉王琰獲高干，以功封侯。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Treatise says: "Shangluo commandant Wang Yan captured Gao Gan—with merit enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Cao Pi's Treatise records that Commandant Wang Yan of Shangluo captured Gao Gan and earned a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 其妻哭於室，以為琰富貴將更娶妾媵故也。」

translations.literal: His wife wept in chamber—thought Yan wealthy noble would again take concubine attendants cause."
translations.idiomatic: His wife wept indoors, thinking Wang Yan meant to trade her for younger wives now that he was rich and titled."

sentences.zh: 十二年，曹操征遼西，擊烏桓。

translations.literal: Twelfth year—Cao Cao campaigned Liaoxi—struck Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Cao Cao campaigned into western Liaoxi against the Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 尚、熙與烏桓逆操軍，戰敗走，乃與親兵數千人奔公孫康於遼東。

translations.literal: Shang, Xi with Wuhuan opposed Cao army—battle defeated fled—thereupon with close troops several thousand fled to Gongsun Kang at Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi joined the Wuhuan against Cao, lost, and fled east with a few thousand household guards to Gongsun Kang in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 尚有勇力，先與熙謀曰：「今到遼東，康必見我，我獨為兄手擊之，且據其郡，猶可以自廣也。

translations.literal: Shang had courage strength—first with Xi plotted saying: "Now arriving Liaodong—Kang surely will see us—I alone for elder brother personally strike him—and seize his commandery—still can self-expand.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang still had fight in him and whispered to Yuan Xi, "Once we reach Liaodong, Kang will receive us—I will strike him down with my own hands, seize his commandery, and carve out a realm.

sentences.zh: 」康亦心規取尚以為功，乃先置精勇於廄中，然後請尚、熙。

translations.literal: " Kang also heart plotted seize Shang for merit—thereupon first placed crack troops in stable—afterward invited Shang, Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Kang planned to deliver Shang's head to Cao; he hid elite troops in his stables before inviting the Yuan brothers inside.

sentences.zh: 熙疑不欲進，尚強之，遂與俱入。

translations.literal: Xi doubted not wishing advance—Shang forced him—thereupon with together entered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xi hesitated but Yuan Shang dragged him forward and both stepped in.

sentences.zh: 未及坐，康叱伏兵禽之，坐於凍地。

translations.literal: Not yet reached sitting—Kang shouted ambush troops seize them—sat on frozen ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could sit, Kang barked an order and hidden guards seized them and forced them onto the frozen earth.

sentences.zh: 尚謂康曰：「未死之閒，寒不可忍，可相與席。

translations.literal: Shang said to Kang: "Between not yet dead—cold unbearable—can mutually share mat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang told Kang, "While we still breathe this cold is unbearable—give us a mat together.

sentences.zh: 」康曰：「卿頭顱方行萬里，何席之為！

translations.literal: " Kang said: "Your heads skulls just about travel ten thousand li—what mat's purpose!
translations.idiomatic: Kang sneered, "Your heads are bound for a journey of ten thousand li—what use is a mat?

sentences.zh: 」遂斬首送之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon beheaded heads sent them.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded them both and sent the heads south.

sentences.zh: 公孫康

translations.literal: Gongsun Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Kang.

sentences.zh: 康，遼東人。

translations.literal: Kang—a Liaodong man.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Kang came from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 父度。

translations.literal: Father Du.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Gongsun Du.

sentences.zh: 初避吏為玄兔小吏，稍仕。

translations.literal: First fled clerk became Xuantu minor clerk—gradually served.
translations.idiomatic: He first fled legal trouble by becoming a petty clerk in Xuantu and slowly rose in office.

sentences.zh: 中平元年，還為本郡守。

translations.literal: Zhongping first year—returned as native commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongping he became governor of his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 在職敢殺伐，郡中名豪與己夙無恩者，遂誅滅百餘家。

translations.literal: In office dared kill strike—within commandery famed stalwarts with self early lacking kindness—thereupon executed extinguished hundred-plus households.
translations.idiomatic: In office he struck without mercy: every powerful clan that had never favored him—more than a hundred households—was extirpated.

sentences.zh: 因東擊高句驪，西攻烏桓，威行海畔。

translations.literal: Thereupon east struck Gaogouli—west attacked Wuhuan—awe traveled sea shore.
translations.idiomatic: He struck east against Gaogouli and west against the Wuhuan until his terror ran along the shore.

sentences.zh: 時王室方亂，度恃其地遠，陰獨懷幸。

translations.literal: At time royal house just chaotic—Du relied on his land remote—secretly alone cherished fortune.
translations.idiomatic: While the court dissolved in chaos, Du trusted his remoteness and secretly harbored ambition.

sentences.zh: 會襄平社生大石丈餘，下有三小石為足，度以為己瑞。

translations.literal: Meeting Xiangping earth-altar produced great stone more than one zhang—below three small stones as feet—Du took as self auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiangping altar sprouted a stone pillar ten feet tall with three small stones for legs, Du read it as heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: [一]初平元年，乃分遼東為遼西、中遼郡，並置太守，越海收東萊諸縣，為營州刺史，[二]自立為遼東侯、平州牧，追封父延為建義侯。

translations.literal: [One] Chuping first year—thereupon divided Liaodong into Liaoxi, Zhongliao commanderies—together established prefects—crossed sea seized Donglai various counties—became Yingzhou Inspector—[two] self-established Liaodong Marquis, Pingzhou Shepherd—retroactively enfeoffed father Yan as Jianyi Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: [One] In the first year of Chuping he split Liaodong into Liaoxi and Central Liaodong, appointed governors, crossed the sea to seize Donglai counties, styled himself inspector of Ying province, [two] proclaimed himself Marquis of Liaodong and shepherd of Pingzhou, and posthumously ennobled his father Yan as Marquis Jianyi.

sentences.zh: 立漢二祖廟。

translations.literal: Established temples to Han's two founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: He erected shrines to the First and Second Founders of Han.

sentences.zh: 承製設□墠於襄平城南，郊祀天地，藉田理兵，乘鸞輅九旒旄頭羽騎。

translations.literal: Receiving forged patent he set up [lacuna] altar-mounds south of Xiangping city, suburban-sacrificed Heaven and Earth, borrowed-field drilled troops, mounted phoenix carriage nine pennants yak-tail vanguard feather riders.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on forged credentials he built suburban altars south of Xiangping, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the borders, opened the sacred field and reviewed troops, and rode in the nine-banner phoenix car with yak-tail escort and plumed horse guards.

sentences.zh: 建安九年，司空曹操表為奮威將軍，封永寧鄉侯。

translations.literal: Jian'an ninth year—Minister of Works Cao Cao memorialized him as General Who Inspires Might—enfeoffed Village Marquis of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 9 Cao Cao secured him the title General Who Inspires Might and Village Marquis of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 度死，康嗣，故遂據遼土焉。

translations.literal: Du died—Kang succeeded—therefore ultimately held Liaodong soil.
translations.idiomatic: When Du died Kang inherited his domain and kept Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 注[一]襄平，縣，屬遼東郡，故城在今平州盧龍縣西南。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Xiangping is a county belonging to Liaodong commandery—the old walls lie southwest of today's Lulong county in Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Xiangping county lay in Liaodong commandery; its ruins are southwest of modern Lulong in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 《魏志》曰：「時襄平延裡社生大石，或謂度曰：『此漢宣帝冠石祥也，裡名與先君同。

translations.literal: Wei Records says: "At that time at Yanli commune in Xiangping a great stone sprouted—someone said to Du: 'This is Han Xuandi's crown-stone omen—the commune name matches your late father's.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Wei note that a pillar of stone rose at Yanli commune outside Xiangping; men told Du it matched Emperor Xuandi's crown-stone portent and echoed his father's placename.

sentences.zh: 社主土地，明當有土地，有三公輔也。

translations.literal: The earth-god masters soil—clearly there shall be territory—having three dukes to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The altar god governs the soil—a sign you will hold land with three great ministers at your side.

sentences.zh: 』度益喜。」

translations.literal: ' Du grew still more pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Du was overjoyed."

sentences.zh: 注[二]為猶置也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Wei means establish.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: wei here means "to establish."

sentences.zh: 劉表字景升，山陽高平人，魯恭王之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Biao styled Jingsheng—a Gaoping man of Shanyang—after Prince Gong of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao (courtesy Jingsheng), a native of Gaoping in Shanyang, descended from Prince Gong of Lu.

sentences.zh: [一]身長八尺餘，姿貌溫偉。

translations.literal: [One] Body length exceeded eight chi—bearing mild grand.
translations.idiomatic: [One] He stood more than eight chi tall and carried himself with gentle dignity.

sentences.zh: 與同郡張儉等俱被訕議，號為「八顧」。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Jian of same commandery and others both suffered malicious criticism—styled "Eight Who Look Back."
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Jian of his commandery were lampooned together and counted among the "Eight Men Who Turned Heads."

sentences.zh: 詔書捕案黨人，表亡走得免。

translations.literal: Edict ordered arrest investigate faction men—Biao fled walked obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When edicts hunted the faction lists he fled and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 黨禁解，辟大將軍何進掾。

translations.literal: Faction prohibition dissolved—summoned General-in-Chief He Jin aide.
translations.idiomatic: After the prohibition lifted He Jin recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 注[一]恭王，景帝子，名余。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Prince Gong—Emperor Jing's son—named Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Prince Gong was Emperor Jing's son Yu.

sentences.zh: 乃使越遣人誘宗賊帥，至者十五人，皆斬之而襲取其觿。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered Yue send men to entice lineage-bandit chiefs—those who arrived fifteen persons—all executed them and surprise seized their armies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kuai Yue to lure the clan bandit chiefs; when fifteen came to parley he slew them all and seized their troops.

sentences.zh: 唯江夏賊張虎、陳坐擁兵據襄陽城，表使越與龐季往譬之，乃降。

translations.literal: Only Jiangxia bandits Zhang Hu and Chen Zuo holding troops occupying Xiangyang city—Biao ordered Yue with Pang Ji to go persuade them—thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Hu and Chen Zuo of Jiangxia still held Xiangyang until Liu Biao sent Kuai Yue and Pang Ji to talk them down.

sentences.zh: 江南悉平。

translations.literal: South of the river all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The land south of the Han River was pacified.

sentences.zh: 諸守令聞表威名，多解印綬去。

translations.literal: Various prefects magistrates hearing Biao's awe-name—many undid seals cords and departed.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates who heard of Liu Biao's renown mostly surrendered their seals and fled.

sentences.zh: 表遂理兵襄陽，以觀時變。

translations.literal: Biao thereupon drilled troops Xiangyang—to observe age's changes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao then exercised his troops at Xiangyang and watched how the times turned.

sentences.zh: 注[一]《王氏譜》曰：「叡字通曜，晉太保祥之伯父也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Wang Clan Register says: "Rui styled Tongyao—Jin Grand Guardian Xiang's uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: the Wang genealogy identifies Wang Rui (courtesy Tongyao) as great-uncle of Wang Xiang, later Grand Tutor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 」《吳錄》曰：「叡見執，驚曰：『我何罪？

translations.literal: " Wu Records says: "Rui seen seized—startled said: 'What crime have I?
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Records add that when seized Wang Rui cried, "What wrong have I done?

sentences.zh: 』堅曰：『坐無所知。

translations.literal: " Jian said: 'Sit knowing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian answered, "Your guilt is ignorance itself.

sentences.zh: 』叡窮迫，刮金飲之而死。」

translations.literal: ' Rui pressed hard—scraped gold drank it and died."
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Wang Rui scraped gold leaf, swallowed it, and died."

sentences.zh: 注[二]宗黨共為賊。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Lineage cliques together became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: clans banded together as outlaws.

sentences.zh: 注[三]宜城，縣，屬南郡，本鄢，惠帝三年改名宜城。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: Yicheng is a county belonging to Nan commandery—originally Yan—Emperor Hui third year changed name Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: Yicheng in Nan commandery was formerly Yan; Emperor Hui renamed it in his third year.

sentences.zh: 注[四]傅子曰：「越字異度，魏太祖平荊州，與荀彧書曰：『不喜得荊州，喜得異度耳。』」

translations.literal: Commentary note [four]: Fu Zi says: "Yue styled Yidu—Wei Grand Progenitor pacified Jingzhou—wrote to Xun Yu saying: 'Not pleased obtaining Jingzhou—pleased obtaining Yidu, that is all.'"
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 4: Fu Xuan quotes Cao Cao's letter to Xun Yu after conquering Jing: "I care less for Jingzhou than for Kuai Yidu."

sentences.zh: 注[五]《漢官儀》曰，荊州管長沙、零陵、桂陽、南陽﹑江*

translations.literal: Commentary note [five]: Han Official Regulations says Jingzhou administered Changsha, Lingling, Guiyang, Nanyang, Jiang—
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 5: Han Official Regulations lists Jingzhou as covering Changsha, Lingling, Guiyang, Nanyang, Jiang—

translations.literal: (ling)
translations.idiomatic: (ling)

sentences.zh: **[夏]*、武陵、南郡、章陵等是也。

translations.literal: **[xia]* and Wuling, Nan commandery, Zhangling and so forth—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: **—xia—plus Wuling, Nan commandery, Zhangling, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 袁術與其從兄紹有隙，而紹與表相結，故術共孫堅合從襲表。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu with his elder cousin Shao had rift—while Shao with Biao mutually bonded—therefore Shu together Sun Jian united alliance raid Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu quarreled with his cousin Yuan Shao, while Shao grew close to Liu Biao—so Shu allied with Sun Jian in a joint strike on Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 表敗，堅遂圍襄陽。

translations.literal: Biao defeated—Jian thereupon surrounded Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao lost the field, and Sun Jian laid siege to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 會表將黃祖救至，堅為流箭所中死，余觿退走。

translations.literal: Meeting Biao general Huang Zu rescue arrived—Jian by flowing arrow struck died—remainder army retreated fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao's general Huang Zu brought relief, a stray arrow killed Sun Jian and his army withdrew.

sentences.zh: [一]及李傕等入長安，冬，表遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: [One] When Li Jue and others entered Chang'an—winter—Biao dispatched envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: [One] After Li Jue's faction seized Chang'an, Liu Biao sent tribute that winter.

sentences.zh: 傕以表為鎮南將軍、荊州牧，封成武侯，假節，以為己援。

translations.literal: Jue appointed Biao General Who Guards the South and Jingzhou Shepherd—enfeoffed Marquis Wucheng of Cheng—borrowed tally—took as self ally.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue named him General Who Guards the South and shepherd of Jing, Marquis Wucheng of Cheng, with ceremonial axe—as his ally.

sentences.zh: 注[一]《典略》曰：「劉表夜遣將黃祖潛出兵，堅逆與戰，祖敗走，竄峴山中。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Dianlue says: "Liu Biao night dispatched general Huang Zu secretly sent troops—Jian met and fought—Zu defeated fled—hid Xian mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Dianlue describes Huang Zu slipping out by night; Sun Jian engaged him; Zu fled into the Xian hills.

sentences.zh: 堅乘勝夜追祖，祖部兵從竹木閒射堅，殺之。

translations.literal: Jian riding victory night pursued Zu—Zu's troops from bamboo trees between shot Jian—killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian pressed the pursuit until Zu's men shot him from cover among bamboo and killed him.

sentences.zh: 」《英雄記》：「劉表將呂介將兵緣山向堅，堅輕騎尋山討介，介下兵射中堅頭，應時物故。

translations.literal: " Records of Heroes: "Liu Biao general Lu Jie led troops along mountain toward Jian—Jian light cavalry sought mountain attacking Jie—Jie's troops shot struck Jian head—on the spot died.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic Tales claims Liu Biao's Lu Jie climbed the heights against Sun Jian; Jian rode light to hunt him down until Jie's archers struck his head—another account of his death.

sentences.zh: 」與此不同。

translations.literal: " Differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: That version disagrees with this narrative.

sentences.zh: 建安元年，驃騎將軍張濟自關中走南陽，因攻穰城，中飛矢而死。

translations.literal: Jian'an first year—Cavalry General Zhang Ji from Guanzhong fled Nanyang—thereupon attacked Rang city—struck flying arrow died.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 1 Zhang Ji fled Guanzhong to Nanyang, attacked Rang, and died from a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 荊州官屬皆賀。

translations.literal: Jingzhou officials all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: His Jingzhou officers hailed the news.

sentences.zh: 表曰：「濟以窮來，主人無禮，至於交鋒，此非牧意，牧受吊不受賀也。」

translations.literal: Biao said: "Ji because destitute came—host lacked ritual—reaching blade clash—this is not shepherd's intent—shepherd accepts condolences not congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao answered, "Zhang Ji came in desperation; we failed him as hosts until blades crossed—that was never my wish. I mourn his death; I do not celebrate it."

sentences.zh: 使人納其觿，觿聞之喜，遂皆服從。

translations.literal: Sent men accept his army—army heard it pleased—thereupon all submitted obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed Zhang Ji's troops; hearing his generosity they all submitted.

sentences.zh: [一]三年，長沙太守張羨率零陵、桂陽三郡畔表，表遣兵攻圍，破羨，平之。

translations.literal: [One] Third year—Changsha prefect Zhang Xian led Lingling, Guiyang three commanderies rebel Biao—Biao dispatched troops attack surround—defeated Xian—pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: [One] In the third year Changsha's Zhang Xian raised Lingling and Guiyang against him; Liu Biao besieged him, broke his lines, and restored order.

sentences.zh: [二]於是開土遂廣，南接五領，[三]北據漢川，地方數千里，帶甲十餘萬。

translations.literal: [Two] Thereupon opened territory became broad—south joined Five Ridges—[three] north occupied Han river territory—land square several thousand li—armored over hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: [Two] His borders stretched south to the Five Ridges [three] and north along the Han valley—thousands of li under arms numbering over one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州人情好擾，加四方駭震，寇賊相扇，處處麋沸。

translations.literal: At first—Jingzhou people's disposition fond disturbance—add four quarters terrified shake—bandits mutually fan—everywhere elk boiling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingzhou seethed with unrest while the realm convulsed—bandits fed one another until every district boiled over.

sentences.zh: 表招誘有方，威懷兼洽，其奸猾宿賊更為效用，萬里肅清，大小鹹悅而服之。

translations.literal: Biao summoned enticed had method—awe cherish together harmonized—those crafty veteran bandits again became useful—ten thousand li solemn clear—great small all salted pleased and submitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao blended kindness with awe until veteran bandits enlisted under his banner; peace ran for myriad li and high and low accepted his rule.

sentences.zh: 關西、兗﹑豫學士歸者蓋有千數，表安慰賑贍，皆得資全。

translations.literal: Guanxi, Yan, Yu scholars returning perhaps thousand count—Biao comforted relief aided—all obtained resources preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of scholars streamed in from Guanxi, Yan, and Yu; Liu Biao fed and clothed them until every refugee found footing.

sentences.zh: 遂起立學校，博求儒術，綦母闓、宋忠等[四]撰立五經章句，謂之後定。

translations.literal: Thereupon erected schools—widely sought Confucian arts—Qi Wu Kai, Song Zhong and others [four] composed established Five Classics chapter-phrases—called Later Fixed.
translations.idiomatic: He founded academies, recruited classicists, and commissioned Qi Wu Kai and Song Zhong [four] to compile chapter-and-verse glosses on the Five Classics—the "Later Recension."

sentences.zh: 愛民養士，從容自保。

translations.literal: Loved people nourished scholars—calm self-preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished the people, kept scholars fed, and guarded his realm at ease.

sentences.zh: 注[一]獻帝春秋曰：「濟引觿入荊州，賈詡隨之歸劉表。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Annals of Emperor Xian says: "Ji led army into Jingzhou—Jia Xu followed returning Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Annals of Emperor Xian records Zhang Ji leading troops into Jing with Jia Xu in tow to serve Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 襄陽城守不受，濟因攻之，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Xiangyang city guard did not accept—Ji thereupon attacked it—by stray arrow struck.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang barred its gates, Zhang Ji assaulted the walls, and fell to a stray shaft.

sentences.zh: 濟從子繡收觿而退。

translations.literal: Ji's nephew Xiu gathered army and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhang Xiu gathered the army and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉表自責，以為己無賓主禮，遣使招繡，繡遂屯襄陽，為表北藩。」

translations.literal: Liu Biao self-blamed—thought self lacked guest-host ritual—sent envoys summon Xiu—Xiu thereupon encamped Xiangyang—as Biao north bulwark."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao blamed himself for discourtesy and summoned Zhang Xiu; Xiu camped at Xiangyang as his northern shield."

sentences.zh: 注[二]《英雄記》曰：「張羨，南陽人。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Records of Heroes says: "Zhang Xian—Nanyang man.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Heroic Tales identifies Zhang Xian as a man of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 先作零陵、桂陽守，甚得江湘閒心。

translations.literal: Formerly served Lingling, Guiyang guard—greatly obtained Jiang-Xiang region hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He had governed Lingling and Guiyang and won the Jiang-Xiang gentry.

sentences.zh: 然性屈強不順，表薄其為人，不甚禮也。

translations.literal: Yet nature stubborn unyielding—Biao slighted his person—not greatly ritual.
translations.idiomatic: But he was stiff-necked; Liu Biao despised his temper and treated him coldly.

sentences.zh: 羨因是懷恨，遂畔表。」

translations.literal: Xian because this harbored hatred—thereupon rebelled Biao."
translations.idiomatic: Xian nursed a grudge and rose against Liu Biao."

sentences.zh: 注[三]裴氏《廣州記》云：「大庾、始安、臨賀、桂陽、揭陽，是謂五領。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: Pei's Guangzhou Record says: "Dayu, Shi'an, Linhe, Guiyang, Jieyang—these are called Five Ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: Pei's Guangzhou Record lists Dayu, Shi'an, Linhe, Guiyang, and Jieyang as the Five Ridges.

sentences.zh: 」鄧德明《南康記》曰：「大庾一也，桂陽甲騎二也，九真都龐三也。

translations.literal: " Deng Deming's Nankang Record says: "Dayu is one—Guiyang armored cavalry is two—Jiuzhen Dupang is three.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Deming's Nankang Record counts Dayu first, Guiyang's armored pass second, Jiuzhen's Dupang third.

sentences.zh: 臨賀萌渚四也，始安越城五也。」

translations.literal: Linhe Mengzhu is four—Shi'an Yuecheng is five."
translations.idiomatic: Linhe's Mengzhu ford fourth and Shi'an's Yuecheng fifth."

sentences.zh: 注[四]闓音開。

translations.literal: Commentary note [four]: Kai is read kai.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 4: Kai is pronounced like kai "open."

sentences.zh: 及曹操與袁紹相持於官度，紹遣人求助，表許之，不至，亦不援曹操，且欲觀天下之變。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao with Yuan Shao faced each other at Guandu—Shao sent men seeking help—Biao promised them—not arrived—also did not aid Cao Cao—and wished to observe realm's changes.
translations.idiomatic: While Cao Cao and Yuan Shao fought at Guandu, Yuan Shao begged help; Liu Biao promised troops but sent none, aided neither side, and waited to see how fortune tilted.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎南陽韓嵩、[一]別駕劉先說表[二]曰：「今豪桀並爭，兩雄相持，天子之重在於將軍。

translations.literal: Attendant Clerk Nanyang Han Song—[one] Adjutant Administrator Liu Xian persuaded Biao—[two] saying: "Now heroes together contend—two stalwarts face each other—the Son of Heaven's weight lies with the general.
translations.idiomatic: Han Song of Nanyang and Liu Xian [one][two] urged him: "Champions tear at each other while two titans lock horns—the emperor's fate hangs on you.

sentences.zh: 若欲有為，起乘其敝可也；

translations.literal: If wishing to have accomplishment—rise seize their exhaustion permissible;
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to seize mastery yourself, strike while they weaken;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，固將擇所宜從。

translations.literal: If not so—firmly will choose what fittingly follow.
translations.idiomatic: if not, you must choose whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 豈可擁甲十萬，坐觀成敗，求援而不能助，見賢而不肯歸！

translations.literal: How can holding armor hundred thousand—sit observe victory defeat—seek rescue yet unable aid—see worthy yet unwilling submit!
translations.idiomatic: How can you arm one hundred thousand men yet sit idle—promise reinforcements you never send and refuse the winning side!

sentences.zh: 此兩怨必集於將軍，恐不得中立矣。

translations.literal: These two resentments surely gather on general—fear cannot obtain neutrality.
translations.idiomatic: Both camps will blame you; neutrality may prove impossible.

sentences.zh: 曹操善用兵，且賢俊多歸之，其埶必舉袁紹，然後移兵以向江漢，恐將軍不能御也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao good at using troops—and worthy talents many submit him—his momentum surely overcomes Yuan Shao—afterward shifts troops toward Jiang Han—fear general unable resist.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao is a master of war and draws worthy men; he will overcome Yuan Shao and then wheel toward the Jiang and Han—you may not withstand him.

sentences.zh: 今之勝計，莫若舉荊州以附曹操，操必重德將軍，長享福祚，垂之後嗣，此萬全之策也。

translations.literal: Now's victorious plan—nothing like raising Jingzhou to attach Cao Cao—Cao surely heavy virtue general—long enjoy blessing mandate—hang to posterity—this ten-thousand-complete strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The safest course is to offer Jingzhou to Cao Cao; he will honor you richly, secure fortune for your heirs—that is the prudent path.

sentences.zh: 」蒯越亦勸之。

translations.literal: " Kuai Yue also urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Yue pressed the same counsel.

sentences.zh: 表狐疑不斷，乃遣嵩詣操，觀望虛實。

translations.literal: Biao fox-doubt not decided—thereupon sent Song go to Cao—observe hope emptiness fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Still unresolved, Liu Biao dispatched Han Song to sound out Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 謂嵩曰：「今天下未知所定，而曹操擁天子都許，君為我觀其釁。」

translations.literal: Saying Song: "Now realm not yet knows what settles—but Cao Cao embraces Son of Heaven capital Xu—you for me observe his cracks."
translations.idiomatic: He told Han Song, "The empire hangs in the balance while Cao holds the emperor at Xu—go read his intentions for me."

sentences.zh: 嵩對曰：「嵩觀曹公之明，必得志於天下。

translations.literal: Song replied: "Song observes Duke Cao's clarity—surely obtain will in world.
translations.idiomatic: Han Song answered, "Cao Gong's clarity marks him for mastery of the realm.

sentences.zh: 將軍若欲歸之，使嵩可也；

translations.literal: General if wishing submit him—send Song permissible;
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to join him, sending me will suffice;

sentences.zh: 如其猶豫，嵩至京師，天子假嵩一職，不獲辭命，則成天子之臣，將軍之故吏耳。

translations.literal: If like hesitant—Song arrives capital—Son of Heaven lends Song one office—not obtain decline mandate—then becomes Son of Heaven's minister—general's former clerk ear.
translations.idiomatic: if you still hesitate and I reach the capital, the emperor may grant me office I cannot refuse—I become the emperor's minister and only your former clerk.

sentences.zh: 在君為君，不復為將軍死也。

translations.literal: At lord is lord—not again for general die.
translations.idiomatic: I would owe my allegiance to him, not die for you alone.

sentences.zh: 惟加重思。

translations.literal: Only add heavy reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh that carefully.

sentences.zh: 」表以為憚使，強之。

translations.literal: " Biao thought him fear envoy—forced him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao mistook his scruples for cowardice and ordered him to go.

sentences.zh: 至許，果拜嵩侍中、零陵太守。

translations.literal: Arrived Xu—indeed appointed Song Palace Attendant, Lingling prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At Xu he was appointed Palace Attendant and prefect of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 及還，盛稱朝廷曹操之德，勸遣子入侍。

translations.literal: When returned—greatly praised court Cao Cao's virtue—urged send son enter attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he praised the court and Cao's virtue and urged Liu Biao to send an heir to Xu.

sentences.zh: 表大怒，以為懷貳，陳兵詬嵩，將斬之。

translations.literal: Biao greatly angry—thought harboring divided loyalty—arrayed troops revile Song—about execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao flew into rage, accused him of treason, lined up troops to revile him, and prepared his execution.

sentences.zh: [三]嵩不為動容，徐陳臨行之言。

translations.literal: [Three] Song not by moved expression—slowly stated departing-time words.
translations.idiomatic: [Three] Han Song never flinched but calmly repeated what he had said before leaving.

sentences.zh: 表妻蔡氏知嵩賢，諫止之。

translations.literal: Biao wife Lady Cai knew Song worthy—remonstrated stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cai knew Han Song's worth and persuaded Liu Biao to stay his hand.

sentences.zh: 表猶怒，乃考殺從行者。

translations.literal: Biao still angry—thereupon interrogated killed followers.
translations.idiomatic: Still furious, Liu Biao tortured Han Song's attendants to death.

sentences.zh: 知無它意，但囚嵩而已。

translations.literal: Knew no other intent—but imprisoned Song only.
translations.idiomatic: Finding no treason in Han Song himself he only imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: [四] 注[一]先賢行狀曰：「嵩字德高，義陽人，少好學，貧不改操。」

translations.literal: [Four] Commentary note [one]: Conduct of Former Worthies says: "Song styled Degao—Yiyang man—young fond study—poverty not change integrity."
translations.idiomatic: [Four] Commentary, note 1: Conduct of Former Worthies describes Han Song (courtesy Degao) of Yiyang as book-loving from youth and incorruptible in poverty."

sentences.zh: 注[二]零陵先賢傳曰：「先字始宗。

translations.literal: Commentary note [two]: Lingling Worthies Biographies says: "Xian styled Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 2: Lingling Worthies gives Liu Xian the courtesy Shizong.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，尤好黃老，明習漢家典故。」

translations.literal: Broad study strong memory—especially fond Huang-Lao—clearly practiced Han house precedents."
translations.idiomatic: Learned, retentive, devoted to Huang-Lao teaching, versed in Han precedent."

sentences.zh: 注[三]詬，罵也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [three]: Gou means revile.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 3: gou means "to revile."

sentences.zh: 注[四]傅子曰：「表妻蔡氏諫之曰：『韓嵩，楚國之望，且其言直，誅之無辭。

translations.literal: Commentary note [four]: Fu Zi says: "Biao wife Lady Cai remonstrated saying: 'Han Song—Chu state's expectation—and his words straight—execute him no excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 4: Fu Xuan records Lady Cai warning that Han Song is Chu gentry's hope and speaks plainly—there is no fair charge for killing him.

sentences.zh: 』表乃不誅而囚之。」

translations.literal: ' Biao thereupon not executed but imprisoned him."
translations.idiomatic: So Liu Biao spared him and kept him in chains."

sentences.zh: 六年，劉備自袁紹奔荊州，表厚相待結而不能用也。

translations.literal: Sixth year—Liu Bei from Yuan Shao fled Jingzhou—Biao thickly treated befriended yet unable use.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Liu Bei fled Yuan Shao for Jingzhou; Liu Biao welcomed him warmly yet never employed his talents.

sentences.zh: 十三年，曹操自將征表，未至。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year—Cao Cao personally led campaign Biao—not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Cao Cao marched against Liu Biao in person but had not arrived.

sentences.zh: 八月，表疽發背卒。

translations.literal: Eighth month—Biao carbuncle erupted back died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Biao died of a back abscess.

sentences.zh: [一]在荊州幾二十年，家無餘積。

translations.literal: [One] At Jingzhou nearly twenty years—house without surplus accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: [One] After nearly twenty years in Jingzhou his household kept no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 注[一]《代語》曰「表死後八十餘年，晉太康中，頤見發，表及妻身形如生，芬香聞數裡」也。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Dai Yu says "After Biao died eighty-plus years—Jin Taikang era—Yi tomb opened—Biao and wife body form like alive—fragrance smell several li"—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Dai Yu adds that eighty years after his death grave robbers in Jin Taikang found Liu Biao and his wife uncorrupted and fragrant for li around.

sentences.zh: 二子：琦，琮。

translations.literal: Two sons—Qi, Cong.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Qi and Cong.

sentences.zh: 表初以琦貌類於己，甚愛之，後為琮娶其後妻蔡氏之侄，蔡氏遂愛琮而惡琦，毀譽之言日聞於表。

translations.literal: Biao at first because Qi appearance resembled self—greatly loved him—afterward for Cong married his later wife Lady Cai's nephew—Lady Cai thereupon loved Cong and hated Qi—slander praise words daily heard by Biao.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Biao doted on Qi for resembling him; later he wed Cong to Lady Cai's niece, whereupon Lady Cai favored Cong and slandered Qi daily in Liu Biao's ear.

sentences.zh: 表寵耽後妻，每信受焉。

translations.literal: Biao doting addicted later wife—each believed accepted thereof.
translations.idiomatic: Besotted with his second wife, Liu Biao believed her every word.

sentences.zh: 又妻弟蔡瑁及外甥張允並得幸於表，又睦於琮。

translations.literal: Also wife younger brother Cai Mao and sister's son Zhang Yun together obtained favor from Biao—and were harmonious with Cong.
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Cai Mao and nephew Zhang Yun also enjoyed Liu Biao's favor and stood close to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 而琦不自寧，嘗與琅邪人諸葛亮謀自安之術。

translations.literal: While Qi did not self tranquil—once plotted with Langye man Zhuge Liang for means self securing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi lived in fear and appealed to Zhuge Liang of Langye for a way to survive.

sentences.zh: 亮初不對。

translations.literal: Liang at first did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang at first stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 後乃共升高樓，因令去梯，謂亮曰：「今日上不至天，下不至地，言出子口而入吾耳，可以言未？

translations.literal: Afterward together ascended tall tower—thereupon ordered remove ladders—said to Liang: "Today above not reach heaven—below not reach earth—words exit your mouth and enter my ears—may speak yet?
translations.idiomatic: Then they climbed a high tower; Qi had the ladders taken away and said, "We stand neither in heaven nor on earth—what leaves your lips enters only my ears—may we speak plainly now?

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「君不見申生在內而危，重耳居外而安乎？

translations.literal: " Liang said: "Have you not seen Sheng within dangerous—and Chong'er dwelling abroad secure?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang replied, "Have you not heard how Prince Sheng perished at court while Chong'er survived in exile?

sentences.zh: 」[一]琦意感悟，陰規出計。

translations.literal: " [One] Qi's intent awakened—secretly planned exit stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: [One] The lesson sank in; Liu Qi secretly laid plans to escape south.

sentences.zh: 會表將江夏太守黃祖為孫權所殺，琦遂求代其任。

translations.literal: Meeting Biao general Jiangxia prefect Huang Zu by Sun Quan killed—Qi thereupon sought substitute his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Zu fell to Sun Quan, Liu Qi asked to take his place at Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 注[一]申生，晉獻公之太子。

translations.literal: Commentary note [one]: Sheng—Jin Duke Xian's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary, note 1: Prince Sheng was heir of Duke Xian of Jin.

sentences.zh: 為麗姬所譖，自縊死。

translations.literal: By Li Ji slandered—self strangled died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ji framed him and he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 重耳，申生之弟。

translations.literal: Chong'er—Sheng's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er was Prince Sheng's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 懼麗姬之讒，出奔。

translations.literal: Fearing Li Ji's slander—fled exile.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing further plots he fled into exile.

sentences.zh: 獻公卒，重耳入，是為文公，遂為霸主。

translations.literal: Duke Xian died—Chong'er entered—this became Duke Wen—thereupon became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: After Duke Xian died Chong'er returned as Duke Wen and rose to hegemony.

sentences.zh: 見《左氏傳》。

translations.literal: Page 2413 line 16 “follow without change”—Wei commentary writes wei “transgress.”
translations.idiomatic: Variant: wei “violate” instead of zun “follow.”

sentences.zh: 二四一四頁三行尚將呂曠高翔魏志「高翔」作「呂翔」，惠棟補注從之。

translations.literal: Page 2414 line 3 Shang generals Lu Kuang and Gao Xiang—Wei Records writes Lu Xiang; Hui Dong’s supplement follows Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Name list harmonized with Wei Records (Lu Xiang).

sentences.zh: 按：潘眉謂作「高翔」是。

translations.literal: Note: Pan Mei argues Gao Xiang is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mei defends the reading Gao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 二四一四頁八行是以周公垂涕以*

translations.literal: Page 2414 line 8 “therefore Duke of Zhou let fall tears to—
translations.idiomatic: Line break before the gloss on bi.

translations.literal: (execute)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: execute.

sentences.zh: **[蔽]*管蔡之獄集解引惠棟說，謂「斃」當作「弊」，斷也。

translations.literal: **cover** Guan-Cai trials—Collected gloss cites Hui Dong: bi should read bi “cut off.”
translations.idiomatic: Hui Dong reads bi as “break off,” not “kill.”

sentences.zh: 或作「蔽」，義同。

translations.literal: Or written bi “screen”; meaning agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Alternate graph bi means shield or screen—same sense.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Text updated per commentary.

sentences.zh: 按：魏志注作「是以周公垂泣而蔽管蔡之獄」。

translations.literal: Note: Wei commentary reads “therefore Duke of Zhou wept while settling the Guan-Cai case.”
translations.idiomatic: Wei quotation prefers “weep” plus bi phrasing.

sentences.zh: 二四一五頁一行貴名*

translations.literal: Page 2415 line 1 “honor name—
translations.idiomatic: Fragment before graph split.

translations.literal: (high)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss: high.

sentences.zh: **[位]*於丘岳據殿本改。

translations.literal: **position** among hills—changed per Palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: Palace edition reads wei “rank” instead of gao.

sentences.zh: 按：校補引錢大昭說，謂閩本「高」作「位」。

translations.literal: Note: Editorial supplement cites Qian Dazhao: Min edition writes wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Dazhao notes Fujian prints read wei.

sentences.zh: 二四一五頁三行匍匐悲號按：「匍匐」二字原倒，逕乙正。

translations.literal: Page 2415 line 3 “crawl and cry”—note: the two graphs were inverted; order corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Characters pufu reversed; sequence fixed.

sentences.zh: 二四一五頁一一行慶父存也按：刊誤謂案公羊云「慶父也存」。

translations.literal: Page 2415 line 11 “Qingfu survives”—errata says Gongyang reads “Qingfu ye survives.”
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang wording differs slightly (ye inserted).

sentences.zh: 二四一六頁五行審配將馮*

translations.literal: Page 2416 line 5 “Shen Pei led Feng—
translations.idiomatic: Name fragment.

translations.literal: (Zha)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss Zha.

sentences.zh: **[禮]*集解引錢大昭說，謂閩本「馮札」作「馮禮」。

translations.literal: **Li**—Collected gloss cites Qian Dazhao: Min edition reads Feng Li.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Dazhao: Feng Li not Feng Zha.

sentences.zh: 又魏志亦作「馮禮」。

translations.literal: Moreover Wei Records also writes Feng Li.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Records agrees on Feng Li.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Adopted Feng Li.

sentences.zh: 按：禮字古作「禮」，形近斗「札」。

translations.literal: Note: Ancient li often looked like zha; easily confused.
translations.idiomatic: Paleographic note on similar shapes.

sentences.zh: 二四一七頁四行相州安*

translations.literal: Page 2417 line 4 “Xiangzhou An—
translations.idiomatic: Place-name fragment.

translations.literal: (yang)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss yang.

sentences.zh: **[陽]*縣界有藍嵯山據殿本改。

translations.literal: **yang** county border has Lancuo mountain—per Palace edition.
translations.idiomatic: Full reading Anyang county with Lancuo; Palace edition.

sentences.zh: 二四一七頁一０行譚夜遁*

translations.literal: Page 2417 line 10 “Tan fled by night—
translations.idiomatic: Verb fragment.

translations.literal: (flee)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss flee.

sentences.zh: **[走]*南皮據汲本改。

translations.literal: **run** to Nanpi—per Ji edition.
translations.idiomatic: Ji edition reads zou “advance” not ben “flee.”

sentences.zh: 按：校補謂奔者逃亡之辭，譚時尚有軍，作「奔」非。

translations.literal: Note: Supplement says ben implies flight; Tan still had an army—ben inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Editor argues ben mischaracterizes a fighting retreat.

sentences.zh: 二四一八頁八行典論曰按：校補引錢大昭說，謂魏志注引此作「典略」。

translations.literal: Page 2418 line 8 “Dianlun says”—note: supplement cites Qian Dazhao: Wei commentary quotes Dianlue.
translations.idiomatic: Title corrected from Dianlun to Dianlue for Wei citation.

sentences.zh: 二四一八頁一四行初避吏為玄兔小吏按：刊誤謂「玄兔」按郡名皆作「菟」。

translations.literal: Page 2418 line 14 “first fled clerks to become Xuantu clerk”—errata: county names should use tu not rabbit.
translations.idiomatic: Standardize Xuantu commandery spelling.

sentences.zh: 二四一九頁四行司空曹操表為奮威將軍按：沈家本謂魏志公孫度傳「奮」作「武」。

translations.literal: Page 2419 line 4 “Minister Cao memorialized Inspire Might”—note: Shen Jiaben says Wei Records Gongsun Du writes Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: Variant general’s title: wuwei vs fenwei.

sentences.zh: 二四二０頁五行至者十五人按：集解引惠棟說，謂司馬彪戰略云「五十五人」。

translations.literal: Page 2420 line 5 “those arriving fifteen”—note: Collected gloss cites Hui Dong: Sima Biao Strategy says fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Number dispute: 15 vs 55 in Strategy.

sentences.zh: 二四二０頁六行唯江夏賊張虎陳坐擁兵據襄陽城按：殿本考證謂何焯校本「坐」改「生」。

translations.literal: Page 2420 line 6 “only Jiangxia bandits Zhang Hu Chen Zuo”—note: Palace critique says He Zhuo’s collation changes zuo to sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Graph zuo vs sheng for Chen’s name.

sentences.zh: 又集解引惠棟說，謂戰略作「陳生」。

translations.literal: Moreover Collected gloss cites Hui Dong: Strategy writes Chen Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Strategy reading Chen Sheng.

sentences.zh: 二四二０頁一三行江*

translations.literal: Page 2420 line 13 “Jiang—
translations.idiomatic: River name fragment.

translations.literal: (ling)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss ling.

sentences.zh: **[夏]*集解引洪亮吉說，謂「江陵」應作「江夏」，表傳凡言江夏者三，漢官儀作「江陵」，誤。

translations.literal: **xia**—Collected gloss cites Hong Liangji: “Jiangling” should be “Jiangxia”; Liu Biao’s biography mentions Jiangxia thrice; Han Official Regulations wrongly writes Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Geographic correction from Jiangling to Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 二四二一頁三行劉表將呂介至應時物故按：校補謂吳志注引英雄記「介」作「公」，「介下兵射中堅頭」作「公兵下石中堅頭」，「應時」下多「腦出」二字。

translations.literal: Page 2421 line 3 “Liu Biao general Lu Jie … died on the spot”—note: supplement says Wu Records Heroic Tales writes jie as gong, changes “Jie’s troops shot Sun Jian’s head” to “Gong’s troops dropped a stone on Sun Jian’s head,” and adds “brains spilled” after “on the spot.”
translations.idiomatic: Wu commentary variant with different name and wound detail.

sentences.zh: 二四二一頁一０行綦母闓按：殿本「綦母」作「綦毋」。

translations.literal: Page 2421 line 10 “Qi Wu Kai”—note: Palace edition writes Qi Wu (different Mu).
translations.idiomatic: Surname variant Qi Wu vs Qi Mu.

sentences.zh: 二四二二頁一０行不獲辭命按：刊誤謂案文當云「辭不獲命」。

translations.literal: Page 2422 line 10 “could not decline mandate”—errata: sentence should read “decline but could not obtain mandate.”
translations.idiomatic: Word order per classical idiom ci bu huo ming.

sentences.zh: 二四二三頁五行代語曰按：校補引錢大昭說，謂代語即世語，唐人避諱改。

translations.literal: Page 2423 line 5 “Daiyu says”—note: supplement cites Qian Dazhao: Daiyu is Shiyu, renamed for Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Tang-period renaming of Shishuo Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 世語晉郭頒撰，隋書經籍志作「魏晉世語」。

translations.literal: Shiyu compiled by Jin Guo Ban; Sui catalogue titles it Wei-Jin Shiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Bibliographic note on Shiyu.

sentences.zh: 二四二四頁一行琦流涕而去人觿聞而傷焉汲本、殿本「人」作「之」，屬上讀。

translations.literal: Page 2424 line 1 “Qi left weeping—people army heard and mourned”—Ji and Palace print zhi, attaching upward.
translations.idiomatic: Punctuation variant: ren vs zhi.

sentences.zh: 按：魏志注引典論，作「琦流涕而去」，無「之」字。

translations.literal: Note: Wei commentary quoting Dianlun reads “Qi left weeping” without zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei text lacks extra graph.

sentences.zh: 二四二四頁八行有知人監識汲本、殿本「監」作「鑒」。

translations.literal: Page 2428 line 8 “know men oversee insight”—Ji and Palace write jian “mirror.”
translations.idiomatic: Graph jian vs jian (mirror).

sentences.zh: 按：監與鑒通。

translations.literal: Note: Jian and jian interchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: Comment on synonymous graphs.

sentences.zh: 二四二四頁一一行劉*

translations.literal: Page 2424 line 11 “Liu—
translations.idiomatic: Surname fragment.

translations.literal: (guang)
translations.idiomatic: Gloss guang.

sentences.zh: **[先]*尚書令按：集解引惠棟說，謂「光」魏志作「先」，即上別駕劉先也。

translations.literal: **Xian** Minister Director—note: Collected gloss cites Hui Dong: Wei Records writes Xian, i.e., Adjutant Liu Xian above.
translations.idiomatic: Identify Liu Xian; Wei uses Xian not Guang.

sentences.zh: 零陵先賢傳亦作「先」。

translations.literal: Lingling Worthies also writes Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Lingling text agrees.

sentences.zh: 今據改。

translations.literal: Now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Use Xian.

sentences.zh: 二四二四頁一一行侍中從事鄧義按：集解引陳景雲說，謂「侍」當作「治」。

translations.literal: Page 2424 line 11 “Palace Attendant clerk Deng Yi”—note: Collected gloss cites Chen Jingyun: shi should be zhi “administrator.”
translations.idiomatic: Office title emended from Palace Attendant to Administrator.

sentences.zh: 又引錢大昕說，謂章懷諱「治」為「持」，此「治中」改「持中」，校書者妄易為「侍」耳。

translations.literal: Moreover cites Qian Daxin: Zhanghuai tabooed zhi as chi—here zhi zhong became chi zhong and copyists wrongly wrote shi.
translations.idiomatic: Taboo chain explaining scribal error.

sentences.zh: 又按：集解引惠棟說，謂魏志「鄧義」作「鄧羲」。

translations.literal: Further note: Collected gloss cites Hui Dong: Wei Records writes Deng Xi for Deng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Name variant Xi vs Yi.
